title: Add release history and per-app version pinning
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
Selecting a published release now opens an explicit version switch, and a successful switch can pin that version. Pinning applies to app updates, Update all and launcher self-update; selecting a release alone changes no installation. History supports pagination, prereleases and retrying temporary GitHub failures.

This is part (a) of the requested split of #141. It follows trusted feed repository renames inside storytold and rechecks GitHub asset URL prefixes when pending-versions.json is loaded, including cached downloads. All installs use main's mandatory SHA-256 verification from #208. Existing install formats, folders and /passive MSI behavior stay in place. The Installation tab only reveals the existing location and uninstall action.

Validation: cargo xtask ci passed on Windows (fmt, Clippy with -D warnings, workspace tests, WASM). Multilingual settings screenshots and regression tests cover pinning, release selection, failed requests and resumed URL validation. No real software was installed during tests.

Follow-ups: Windows portable ZIP support in #217 (draft, depends on this PR); quiet MSI installs and downgrade recovery in #218 (draft, depends on #217). Native macOS/FreeBSD installer validation remains outstanding.

title: Add Windows portable ZIP installations
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
Dependency: [#216](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/pull/216). This PR is rebased on #216, which is rebased on main 0.4.1 (FigCraft). It targets upstream main, so GitHub currently shows the prerequisite commit too. Review the isolated change here: [portable ZIP changes only](https://github.com/Skyfuller1303/craft-launcher/compare/feat/version-history-pinning...feat/windows-portable-zip). After the prerequisite merges, rebase onto updated main.

Windows tools can now install and switch versions from portable ZIP assets. New installations offer a plain text parent-folder field; existing portable installations keep their format and location. Verified executable VERSIONINFO must match the selected release.

This is part (b) of #141, stacked on version history and pinning. Replacement backs up recorded files and rolls back on replacement, verification or manifest-save failure, preserving unrecorded user files. ZIP paths, duplicate names and collisions are rejected. Host directory links are canonicalized, while symlinks/junctions inside launcher-owned directories are rejected. Regression tests cover /home-like ancestor links, owned links and dangling links. No rfd dependency or runtime libdbus backend is added.

title: fix(macos): prompt for administrator access on shared updates
author: bentownsend0
body:
When a standard macOS account updates a Craft app already installed in `/Applications`, copying the staged bundle fails with `Permission denied`. Request macOS administrator authorization for that shared update, including ArtCraft Launcher self-updates, while keeping the existing personal-folder fallback for new installs.

The authorized transaction is limited to known catalog bundles directly in a root/admin-managed `/Applications` folder. It copies into private root-owned staging, rechecks the Developer ID team, bundle ID and version, and preserves the previous app if activation or rollback fails. It rejects symlinks and customized parent ACLs, quotes paths as data, and leaves credentials to the system authorization dialog.

Cancelling the prompt leaves the installed app untouched. Record the self-update suppression marker only after successful installation and restart scheduling so failed or cancelled attempts can be retried immediately. The macOS test DMGs now use HFS+, matching release packaging.

Validation:

- `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo xtask ci` passed: formatting, workspace clippy, 297 tests, and WebAssembly checks. Three existing tests remain ignored.
- Committed regression tests cover authorization cancellation, permission routing, signature/identity/version rejection, path quoting, symlinks, ACLs, rollback failures, concurrent destination changes and self-update retry suppression.
- Independent fixture checks passed 21 transaction cases; the AppleScript wrapper was compiled without executing it.

The live administrator-approved replacement of an installed production app was not exercised. The authorized subprocess is awaited through completion; forcibly quitting the launcher may leave its system prompt or transaction running.

title: Linux: install, update and remove through PackageKit when it carries the app
author: plusky
body:
Linux: install, update and remove through PackageKit when it carries the app

Wherever `pkcon` is available and the distro carries the app, use the
distro's own package instead of the release's file: `pkcon resolve`
over the usual candidate names, then `pkcon install` on a hit and the
old download flow on a miss; distro-owned copies (dpkg/rpm DB match,
no launcher record) update with `pkcon update`, and Deb/Rpm copies
remove with `pkcon remove`. PackageKit authenticates itself through
polkit, so no pkexec wrapper; batched jobs still share one call so
auth is asked once.

Why: the distro's signature instead of ours, real dependency
resolution, system-wide updates through the distro's own process (no
duplicate copies beside the managed one), and the distro's security
process for the package. Zero behavior change where the distro
carries no such package (resolve miss falls through to the old flow
byte-for-byte) or where `pkcon` is absent (existing per-manager
paths stay as the fallback). AppImage/Flatpak copies keep updating
in place and are never doubled by a distro package.

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately

title: WSL: claim a separate single-instance port so the Windows launcher still opens
author: PistachioCannoli
body:
Fixes #271.

### What

Inside WSL, the Linux launcher now claims single-instance port **47414** instead of 47413. Everywhere else (Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, Linux outside WSL) nothing changes.

### Why

WSL shares loopback ports with Windows: WSL 2 (NAT mode) forwards a port a Linux process listens on to the Windows host's loopback, and WSL 1 binds Windows' own. So with a launcher open in WSL, the Windows launcher couldn't bind 47413, said hello to the *Linux* launcher, got `running 0.3.2`, deferred and exited 0 without a window. And because the handshake compares versions, a newer launcher on either side would have made the other quit.

### How

- `in_wsl()` (Linux only): `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` is set, or `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease` contains `microsoft` (WSL 2: `…-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, WSL 1: `…-Microsoft`). The kernel check also covers processes that don't inherit the WSL variables, such as systemd units.
- `port()` → `port_for(in_wsl())`, and `claim()` uses it.
- When a start defers, it now logs `ArtCraft Launcher is already running (port …); asked it to show its window`. Before, it exited silently, which made #271 hard to see.

### Compatibility

- The handshake is unchanged, so every launcher version still works with every other on the same OS. The Windows launcher doesn't need an update for this.
- Self-update isn't affected: its helper waits for the old launcher to exit before starting the new one.
- One transitional case: if you start a launcher with this change by hand in WSL while a 0.3.2-or-older one is still open there, they're on different ports, so you get two WSL launcher windows. This stops once the old one has updated.

### Testing

On Windows 11 25H2 (10.0.26200) with WSL 2.3.26 (NAT mode) and Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.98.1:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass. I didn't run `cargo xtask wasm` locally (no `wasm32` target installed); only `crates/native` changed, and…

title: Harden release-metadata handling and bound resource use
author: JeremyYao
body:
Five small, defensive fixes to how the launcher treats release metadata and remote content, each with a regression test. Normal use is unchanged: apps still list, download, verify, install, and self-update, and a legitimately configured proxy still works.

Validated locally: `cargo test` (core, native, ui-egui), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` check for core + web all pass.

## Changes

1. **Download/link trust was a prefix check that `..` defeats** (`crates/core/src/release.rs`, `crates/core/src/feed.rs`). An asset `download_url` or `html_url` from the feed or the GitHub API was accepted whenever it *started with* `https://github.com/<repo>/releases/...`. A value such as `.../storytold/<app>/releases/download/../../../other-account/<repo>/...` passed that check, and a URL parser (a browser opening the link, or the server) then resolves it back out of the app's own repository. The traversal check that the local-mirror branch already had is now applied to the GitHub branch too, for both plain and percent-encoded sequences, plus `..` in a redirect tag.

2. **Release-notes "Full Changelog" link accepted any scheme** (`crates/ui-egui/src/notes.rs`). The text after `**Full Changelog**: ` in a release body (remote, attacker-influenceable) was handed straight to `hyperlink_to`, so a body could make it a `javascript:`, `data:`, or `file:` link. The link is now created only for `https://` URLs; GitHub's generated changelog line always is one, so the normal case is unaffected.

3. **Small-response cap counted compressed bytes** (`crates/native/src/http.rs`). `MAX_SMALL` was enforced by ureq's limit on the *compressed* source, so a gzip-encoded reply could expand far past the cap in memory before it tripped. The decoded size is now bounded directly, whatever the `Content-Encoding`. The streaming download path was already bounded and is unchanged.

4. **A SOCKS proxy from the environment was silently bypassed** …

title: Open a Craft App with its control channel, for agents
author: smyrgeorge
body:
Every Craft App serves JSON lines on a loopback port when it's started with `--control`, so an agent can drive its window while you watch. This lets the launcher start an app that way, set per app and off by default.

## What changes

- **The `…` menu** of each app has an **Agent control** switch. Switched on, it shows the port the app will listen on. Hover the port for the full address and, for PhotoCraft and PdfCraft, the file holding the token. The menu now stays open on a click inside it, so the port appears as soon as the switch is on. Every existing menu item still closes it.
- **The details drawer** has an **Agent control** box with the same switch, plus the port to change. The drawer's own `…` menu leaves the switch out, the way it leaves out the links it already shows as buttons.
- **Opening the app** adds the arguments that app expects (`core::control`):

| App | Opened with | What an agent needs |
|---|---|---|
| PhotoCraft | `--control <port> --control-token-file <file>` | The token in `<file>` (without a file, PhotoCraft prints its token to standard error, which the launcher discards) |
| PdfCraft | `--control <file>` | The port and token PdfCraft writes to `<file>` (it picks its own port) |
| The other ten | `--control <port>` | The port (WordCraft also writes a key to its own settings folder) |

I checked each app's `main.rs` and control server on `main`. Each app gets its own default port, 7878 upward in suite order (PhotoCraft 7878, VectorCraft 7879, …, SoundCraft 7889), so they can all be open for agents at once. The apps' own docs reuse some ports, e.g. 7979 for VectorCraft and GridCraft. Files go in `control/` in the launcher's data folder.

- **Flatpak:** the app is also run with `--share=network`. Otherwise its loopback is its own and host agents can't reach it; PhotoCraft's manifest deliberately doesn't grant network. Its file goes in `~/.var/app/<id>/`, the one host folder its sandbox sees.

title: macOS: put the app icon on its own squircle tile
author: sajibsrs
body:
Fixes #293

## Problem
On macOS 26 the Dock showed the launcher on a grey tile while it was closed, then as the bare blue "A" once it was running. The bundle's `.icns` was the bare mark on a transparent background. macOS 26 treats that as a legacy icon and only adds its own tile while the app is closed. The runtime isn't involved: eframe 0.36.2 skips the empty `IconData` we pass on macOS.

## Change
- `packaging/icons.sh`: render the macOS icon as the untouched mark on a light squircle tile laid out on Apple's 1024 grid (an 824 px tile with ~185 px corners). The trademark artwork itself is not redrawn, recoloured or cropped.
- Regenerated `assets/app-icon/artcraft-launcher.icns` and `artcraft-launcher-1024.png`. The `.ico` and hicolor PNGs came out byte-identical, so Windows, Linux and BSD are unchanged.
- `assets/app-icon/README.md`: describe the new 1024 px render.

## Testing
Built with `packaging/macos/package.sh --arch aarch64`, installed in `/Applications` and restarted the Dock. The icon is the same closed and running on macOS 26.

title: Add an update service so app updates need no UAC prompt each time
author: Slopapalooza
body:
## Summary

On Windows every Craft App installs for all users, into Program Files, so each update runs its MSI with a UAC prompt. This adds the opt-in **ArtCraft Launcher Update Service**: an administrator installs it once, and from then on app updates install without a prompt.

- **Background updates**: a LocalSystem Windows service checks every 6 hours. Once an administrator turns on automatic updates, it also installs them for the apps installed for all users, leaving any app that's open until it's closed.
- **No UAC per update**: the launcher hands an update to the service when it answers, and shows its progress as before. Without the service, nothing changes: the launcher installs it itself, with the prompt.
- **Command line** (on `PATH`): `artcraft-launcher-updater check | update [APP...] | status | set auto-update on|off`, with `--json` for scripts. `check` exits 100 when updates are available.

## Who controls background installs

They're one setting for the whole computer, and only administrators can change it (`AutoUpdate` in HKLM, `crates/native/src/policy.rs`):

- While the service is installed, the launcher's **Settings → Updates → Automatically download and install updates** shows the computer's setting. Changing it either way takes a UAC prompt. A standard user needs an administrator's password.
- An administrator can also use `artcraft-launcher-updater set auto-update on|off` in an elevated terminal, `AUTOUPDATE=1` on the MSI, or Group Policy. A Group Policy value greys out the checkbox and shows "Set by your administrator."
- Nothing a client sends to the service can change it. It's off until an administrator turns it on.

## What the service will and won't do

It runs as LocalSystem, so it's deliberately narrow:

- It only **updates** apps an administrator already installed for all users, and only to a **newer** release. Installing a new app still goes through the launcher and its UAC prompt.
- Before running a package it checks:
  - the release's …

title: Fetch Linux AppImage updates as zsync deltas
author: PanDuroDev
body:
Closes #320.

## Problem

Every Craft app ships nearly daily, and each update re-downloads the full installer
(`install::download` always fetched the whole asset). Meanwhile every AppImage release
already publishes a `.zsync` control file that `platform.rs` deliberately skipped.

## What this does

Linux AppImage updates now fetch only the blocks that changed:

- `core::delta`: a pure decision (Linux + AppImage + installed copy + listed `.zsync`,
  anything else is `Full`), next to `Platform::default_kinds`. No I/O, wasm-safe.
- `Release::zsync_asset_for`: finds the `.zsync` sibling by exact asset name only, so one
  architecture can never borrow another's control file.
- `native::delta_fetch`: parses the control file, reuses matching blocks from the installed
  copy (exact positions first, then a rolling scan for moved blocks; every weak hit is
  MD4-confirmed), range-fetches only the rest, assembles into a temporary file.
- `install::download` tries the delta first and falls back to the existing full path on
  anything it cannot do. Pause and cancel propagate unchanged and never become a hidden
  full download. Self-updates stay full downloads on purpose (replacing the running binary
  is risky enough).

## What it does not do

- No behaviour change on Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, or for MSI/DMG/deb/rpm/Flatpak/tarball:
  they all answer `Full`, exactly as today.
- No new UI strings, so no `i18n` catalog updates in this PR.

## Security

- MD4 is content matching for zsync compatibility only, never the security check. The
  assembled file is verified against the release's published SHA-256 exactly like a full
  download (#90), and any mismatch deletes the temporary file.
- New `md4` dependency (RustCrypto) for that matching: flagging it here as a maintainer
  call per AGENTS.md.

## Verification

- The `.zsync` format was reverse-engineered from a real published file (PhotoCraft
  v0.8.2's AppImage) and byte-verified against real blocks fetched with Range requests
  b…

title: macOS: quit through terminate: so quitting doesn't crash (#333)
author: jmacek
body:
Fixes #333.

On macOS, every real quit (tray Quit, a newer Launcher taking over, self-update) sent `ViewportCommand::Close`. eframe then drops the window inside AppKit's run loop, and when the window was focused AppKit threw in `-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]` (EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP), the same crash as storytold/craft-libs#3.

This calls `craft_quit::on_close_request(ctx)` at the end of `Shell::logic`, from craft-libs `craft-quit` (storytold/craft-libs#5, pinned to `main` at `f58bc1a`). On macOS it cancels the close and quits through `-[NSApplication terminate:]` instead. Elsewhere it does nothing. It runs last, so a close that the Launcher puts away in the tray (`CancelClose`) is left alone. PdfCraft is adopting the same call in storytold/pdfcraft#1533.

The change is 1 line in `main.rs` plus the dependency. New in `Cargo.lock`: only `craft-quit`; everything it uses was already there.

## Tested

MacBookPro17,1, macOS 26.5.2, release build:
- **Before (installed 0.4.0):** with the window in front, a fake newer-Launcher handshake (`printf 'artcraft-launcher:hello 9.9.9' | nc -w 3 127.0.0.1 47413`) crashes it with EXC_BREAKPOINT.
- **After:**
  - The same handshake quits with exit 0 and no crash report.
  - The red X still hides the window to the tray, and the tray icon brings it back.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher --all-targets -D warnings` are clean. `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher` passes (35 tests).
- I didn't run `cargo xtask wasm` locally because the target isn't installed, but this only touches the native app crate.

title: Sharpen text and lines in the Windows launcher
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
## Problem

On Windows at 100 % scaling, text in the launcher looked soft. The small Geist Mono labels were hit hardest: numbers, `INSTALL`, `AVAILABLE TO INSTALL`. Hairlines were blurred too.

There were two separate causes:

1. **The whole frame was stretched vertically.** egui-winit turns on winit's undecorated-window drop shadow for our borderless window. That hack moves the client area down 1 px (`WM_NCCALCSIZE`). A Direct3D 12 swapchain made straight from the HWND is then scaled by DWM over that area, so the image is resampled vertically by about one row. Every horizontal edge, hairline and line of text ends up half on two pixel rows, and the offset grows further down the window.
   - Measured on the live window: horizontal hairlines that were split over two rows went from 5/10 to 0/9.
   - With native decorations, with Vulkan or GL, or with the shadow switched off, it was already sharp. Only DX12 combined with the borderless shadow was affected.
2. **Glyphs were placed at quarter-pixel x offsets** (egui's subpixel binning). Inter, Archivo and Geist Mono have no horizontal hinting, so at 1× a fractional x spreads each vertical stem across two columns.

In the same area: the card's hover rule ran 1 px over the hairlines it shares with its neighbours, on both sides. On getartcraft.com the rule sits within the grid gaps.

## Changes

- `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs`: on Windows, DX12 presents through DirectComposition (`Dx12SwapchainKind::DxgiFromVisual`). The borderless window keeps its drop shadow. `WGPU_DX12_PRESENTATION_SYSTEM` still overrides it.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`: `subpixel_binning: Some(false)` for the bundled faces, so glyphs land on whole pixels.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/views.rs`: the hover rule is drawn inside the card's 1 px hairlines.

## Screenshots

Real Windows 11 window, 1920×1080 at 100 %, English UI, DX12. These are live window captures, not kittest renders: the vertical stretch only happens in a real swapchain.

title: Linux: repair a Flatpak bundle whose origin remote is gone before updating it (#326)
author: tydude001
body:
Fixes #326

A Flatpak bundle install adds a `<name>-origin` remote to the user's Flatpak config. When two bundle installs run at the
same time, as they did before the installer queue (#149, #153), one can drop the other's remote. The app stays installed,
but every later `flatpak install --reinstall --bundle` of it fails with `Remote "<name>-origin" not found` until the user
uninstalls it and installs it again by hand.

Before installing a Craft App's bundle, the launcher now compares `flatpak info --user --show-origin <id>` with
`flatpak remotes --user`. If the bundle's own `-origin` remote is missing, it uninstalls the app first, so the bundle
installs fresh. The app's settings and data in `~/.var/app` stay, because `--delete-data` isn't passed.

- `packages::origin_remote_missing` only reacts to a bundle's `-origin` remote. If the user removed a real repository
  (Flathub), nothing is uninstalled.
- The check and the uninstall run inside the installer queue, before the install itself.
- `install_package` takes the bundle's app id. Self-update passes `None`, so the launcher never uninstalls the copy
  that's running it.
- If the check can't run (`flatpak info` fails, as it does for an app that isn't installed yet) or the uninstall fails,
  the install goes ahead as before. A failed uninstall is logged.
- One trade-off: if the install that follows the uninstall fails, the app is left uninstalled instead of stuck on its old
  version. A failed install keeps the download, so the next **Install** doesn't fetch it again.

Checks: `cargo xtask ci` passes all four steps (fmt, clippy, test, wasm), with a new unit test for
`origin_remote_missing`.

Tested on Bazzite 44 (Flatpak 1.18.4) with the release binaries, each run with its own `FLATPAK_USER_DIR`. PhotoCraft
0.7.0 was installed from its bundle and then had its `photocraft-origin` remote removed. Then it was updated with its
card's **Update to 0.8.2** button:

title: macOS: mount release disk images under $TMPDIR, not the cache folder (#336)
author: alexisskeates
body:
Fixes #336.

### Cause

`install_dmg` attached every release image at a mount point inside the launcher's cache folder,
`~/Library/Caches/ArtCraft Launcher/mount-<app>-<pid>-<nanos>`. When the user's home folder lives
on an external drive, hdiutil refuses a custom mount point there:

```
hdiutil: attach failed - Permission denied
```

while attaching the same image without `-mountpoint` works. Self-update goes through the same
function, so the launcher could neither install Craft Apps nor update itself on such a Mac.

### Change

- The per-attempt mount folder now lives under `std::env::temp_dir()` (the per-user `$TMPDIR`
  under `/var/folders`, on the boot volume) instead of `paths.cache`. The unique
  `mount-<app>-<pid>-<nanos>` name, the `DISK_IMAGES` mutex, the retry loop and the
  detach/remove cleanup are unchanged. `install_dmg` no longer needs `&Paths`, so that parameter
  is gone (one call site in `install`, one in `self_update`).
- If hdiutil still refuses the mount point, the image is attached without `-mountpoint` (same
  `-nobrowse -readonly -noautoopen -noverify`) plus `-plist`, and the mount path is read from the
  `system-entities` array in hdiutil's output. If that output names no mount point the devices it
  lists are detached again and the install fails with a clear error, so nothing is left attached.
- `diskutil image attach` was deliberately not used: it only exists on recent macOS and the
  launcher supports 11 Big Sur and later.
- No user-facing strings changed (the one error text that moved, "unusual characters in the
  temporary folder's path", is an internal `Err` string in `native`, not an i18n row).
- Doc comments on `install_dmg` and the new `attach` helper describe both paths.

### Tests

- `the_mount_point_is_read_from_hdiutils_plist`: parses a captured `hdiutil attach -plist`
  document, and junk / empty output yields nothing without panicking.

title: Linux: show the tray icon in the Flatpak (#322)
author: tydude001
body:
Fixes #322

Inside the Flatpak the launcher never shows a tray icon, on any desktop. ksni (tray-icon's Linux backend) first asks for
the bus name `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-<n>`, and the sandbox may not own it: Flatpak's D-Bus proxy answers the
`RequestName` with `ServiceUnknown`, and the launcher logs `no tray icon`. tray-icon 0.26.1 (tauri-apps/tray-icon#379)
registers under the connection's unique name when it runs sandboxed, which the watcher accepts. This updates tray-icon
from 0.25.1 to 0.26.1.

tray-icon 0.26 also changes what happens with no StatusNotifierWatcher on the bus (tauri-apps/tray-icon#372). Building
the icon now succeeds, and the icon registers if a watcher appears later. The launcher took "there's a tray icon" to
mean "there's a tray to come back from". On a desktop with no watcher (plain GNOME without the AppIndicator extension),
closing the window would leave the launcher running with no icon and no window. So:

- `Tray::shown` asks the session bus whether `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` has an owner (always true on Windows and
  macOS).
- The close button and the two places that handle a hidden start at login use it in place of `tray.is_some()`. So with
  no watcher, closing quits and a hidden start shows the window, as with 0.25.
- If the watcher appears later, the icon still turns up, and closing goes to the tray from then on.

`with_icon_as_template` is deprecated in 0.26, so macOS uses `with_icon_templated`. In the lockfile, muda goes
from 0.20.0 to 0.21.2, and `libxdo`, `libxdo-sys` and `x11` drop out (muda 0.21 has no libxdo feature). Nothing else changes.

Checks: `cargo xtask ci` passes all four steps (fmt, clippy, test, wasm) on Linux. I couldn't compile for macOS or
Windows here.

Tested on Bazzite 44 (Flatpak 1.18.4) with release builds. KDE's watcher (kded6, plasma-workspace 6.7.5) ran on a
private session bus. The sandboxed runs used the published 0.4.0 Flatpak's sandbox, whose D-Bus permissions `main`
still has, with each …

title: Make the launcher the suite's keychain
author: wdunn001
body:
﻿## What this does

Makes ArtCraft Launcher the Craft App Suite's keychain. Somebody signs in once in the launcher. Every Craft App then uses that session.

## Why

A Craft App keeps its CollabCraft session in its own folder today. GridCraft's lives in `%APPDATA%\GridCraft\collabcraft-session.json`. Taken across the suite that becomes a sign-in per application, a copy of a bearer token on disk per application, and a separate place to revoke per application.

`craft_ui::account::AccountMenu` already holds a list of accounts. The control was therefore ready for this. The store behind it is what was missing.

## The store

A new crate, `artcraft-suite-account`. It has two halves, kept deliberately apart.

The list of accounts is a small JSON file in one suite-level folder:

| Platform | Folder |
|---|---|
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\ArtCraft\accounts.json` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/ArtCraft/accounts.json` |
| Linux, the BSDs | `~/.config/artcraft/accounts.json` |

It is suite-level because an account belongs to the person. `craft-settings` gives each application `<platform config dir>/<app id>`, the right home for that application's own preferences. An account placed under one of those would make every other application read a folder it does not own. Removing that application would then sign everybody out. The launcher's own folder fails for the same reason: an application must not have to know the launcher exists. `ARTCRAFT_SUITE_DIR` overrides the folder. Set and empty means this process reads and writes nothing.

The file holds no credential. It carries the deployment URL, the OIDC subject, a display name, an address and two timestamps, plus which account is active. A test asserts the token never reaches it.

The token goes in the operating system's keychain:

```text
service  ai.storyteller.artcraft.suite-account
user     the account handle: the first 12 bytes of SHA-256(service + "\n" + subject), in hex
secret   the CollabCraft session token, as return…

title: Fix macOS installs on external drives and save DMGs to Downloads
author: LaughingInPurgatory
body:
DMG installs and updates fail with `hdiutil: attach failed - Permission denied` when the launcher's home/cache directory is on an external volume mounted with ownership disabled (`noowners`). Mount each image in a new, private directory under `/private/tmp` on the boot volume instead. Use `diskutil image attach` where supported, retaining `hdiutil` for macOS 11/12. This shared path covers Craft App installs, app updates, and launcher self-updates.

Save macOS DMGs and resumable downloads in the user's Downloads folder, and retain completed DMGs after installation. Keep automatic stale-file cleanup confined to the launcher's cache. The existing checksum, signing-team, version, and staged replacement checks remain in place.

Validation: reproduced the exact reported error on a `noowners` external home volume. The new real-DMG update regression failed before the fix and passes afterward. `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed on macOS: formatting, workspace Clippy, workspace tests, and both WebAssembly checks. Rust 1.95 satisfies the existing pinned egui dependencies; no dependency versions changed. Added checks for private, unique mount directories and the macOS Downloads destination.

title: fix(update): a Flatpak-installed launcher gets the bundle download link, not the AppImage
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What

When the launcher runs as a Flatpak and a new release lands, the update banner/dialog shows a **Download** button (Flatpak copies can't self-update) whose link opened the **AppImage** asset — replacing the sandboxed install's update with a totally different package format.

## Why

`launcher_download` picked from `[AppImage, Deb]` for every Linux copy, ignoring how this copy is actually installed. A sandboxed (Flatpak) copy therefore got an AppImage URL as its "update", and anything unparseable fell through to the generic release page. The install-format signal the picker was missing is the same one the app-install path already uses: `settings::is_flatpak_sandbox()`.

## Change

- `launcher_download(r, p, flatpak)` now takes how this copy is installed (call sites pass `settings::is_flatpak_sandbox()`, the existing check) and, on a sandboxed Linux copy, returns the `.flatpak` bundle asset — no bundle in the release, no link (falls back to the release page, not a foreign format).
- Flag passed explicitly so the picker is a pure function with unit tests, instead of the env read it can't inject.
- Deleted the dead duplicate of `launcher_download` in `native/src/backend.rs` (zero call sites; a stale copy of exactly this logic that would keep drifting).

Tests cover both branches: a Flatpak copy gets the bundle, a plain Linux copy still gets the AppImage.

## Related but different

#190 teaches the Flatpak copy to *self-update* (install, exec, restart); it's still open and untouched by this fix. This PR only fixes the download-link fallback that every Flatpak install gets today.

title: Settings: an Interface size row, and Ctrl + wheel zooms the launcher
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #25 and the whole-interface half of #302. (#351 covers the other half, zooming the release notes on their own.)

egui already scales the launcher with Ctrl +, Ctrl − and Ctrl 0 (⌘ on macOS), and eframe remembers the zoom between runs, but nothing in the launcher says so, and there is no way to do it with the mouse. #25 asks for a setting; #302 asks for Ctrl + wheel.

## Settings → Appearance → Interface size

A row with **−**, the current zoom as a percentage, and **+**. The buttons step by a tenth through `egui::gui_zoom::zoom_in` / `zoom_out`, so they do exactly what Ctrl + and Ctrl − do; clicking the percentage goes back to 100%. Under it, a muted line names the keys and the wheel, with ⌘ on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. The line is left out where egui leaves zooming to the browser (the web build), since the keys belong to the browser there.

## Ctrl + mouse wheel

`LauncherUi::ui` reads `zoom_delta()` each frame (Ctrl + wheel, or a trackpad pinch, as egui reads them) and applies it to the zoom factor within egui's own 0.2–5.0 bounds. Only where `zoom_with_keyboard` is on, for the same reason as above.

Nothing new is persisted: the zoom lives in egui's options, which eframe already saves, so what the keys set and what the row sets are one value.

## Strings

Two new strings and one hover text go through i18n with rows in all ten complete catalogs (cs, de, es, fr, hu, ja, pl, pt-BR, ru, zh-CN); the i18n completeness test passes. The hint keeps a `{mod}` placeholder in every language.

## Test

`the_interface_size_is_stepped_in_settings_and_zoomed_with_the_wheel` opens Settings, checks + gives 110%, the percentage resets to 100%, − gives 90%, a ⌘-wheel event zooms, and egui's ⌘ 0 resets. A snapshot (`settings-interface-size`) shows the row at 110%.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Self-update: a launcher that updates in the tray restarts into the tray
author: XianZheYang
body:
The second complaint in #337: with automatic updates on, a launcher that updates itself while it sits in the tray restarts into a window, over whatever the user is doing. The same happens to a launcher started hidden at login that then updates itself.

## Change

- `Host::window_hidden()` (default `false`, so the web build is untouched): the desktop shell sets it when the window is hidden to the tray or closed to it, cleared when it is shown again, and set while the launcher carries on without a window.
- `Command::UpdateLauncher { restart_hidden }`: automatic updates pass `window_hidden()` along; "Update and restart" in the banner and in the update dialog pass `false`, since the user is looking at the window.
- `self_update::update` takes it to the restart: `--hidden` on Linux (AppImage or package), `open … --args --hidden` on macOS, and `-ArgumentList '--hidden'` on Windows (MSI and portable). `--hidden` is the flag the login item already uses, so the new launcher starts the way it does at login: window created invisible where it can hide, tray-only where it can't, and a window after all when there is no tray to come back from.

The flag is fixed when the update is queued. A window hidden after the download started still comes back; that is the rare case, and the common one (the launcher idle in the tray for hours when a check finds an update) is the one this fixes.

## Tests

- `windows_script` (the helper's PowerShell, now a pure function) ends in `-ArgumentList '--hidden'` only when asked; on Linux `restart_command` appends the flag.
- The shell's unit tests check `window_hidden()` follows `put_away` and `show`.
- A UI test with a host whose window is hidden checks the automatic update sends `UpdateLauncher { restart_hidden: true }`; the existing tests check the clicked paths send `false`.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Windows: detect explicitly registered external apps
author: JamesTsetsekas
body:
Windows copies extracted from the official portable ZIPs into custom folders currently appear as “not installed,” even when their executables already exist. This adds an optional `external-apps.json` registration file: an app ID, absolute executable path and optional version let ArtCraft Launcher detect and open the existing copy.

The file is read only on Windows, with a 64 KiB limit and executable-name validation. Launcher-owned records and MSI detection retain precedence. Without the file, detection and installation defaults are unchanged. Registered copies stay externally managed: they can be opened or revealed, but are excluded from update, reinstall, uninstall, automatic-update and update-notification actions. Passive installed/latest-version information remains visible.

This complements the portable install/location work in #282, #345 and #346 by handling copies already unpacked and maintained outside the launcher. It adds no folder scan, install format, ownership adoption or registry entries. The README documents the opt-in format for installed and portable launchers.

Validation:

title: Title bar: maximized, the close button takes the screen's corner
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #374: with the window maximized on Windows, a click at the very top-right pixel of the screen did nothing, and the cursor had to come a few pixels in before the close button took it.

## Cause

Each window button in the custom title bar keeps the resize band (5 px along the top, and for Close the right edge too) out of its clickable area, so that band stays free for `window_edges` to resize from. `window_edges` rightly does nothing while the window is maximized or full screen, but the buttons kept leaving the band out, so at the screen's corner it belonged to nobody. egui's click tolerance covers a point up to 5 px from a widget, which is why only the extreme corner (about 7 px away diagonally) failed.

## Change

`widgets::resize_band` is the band's width right now: `RESIZE_EDGE` while the window can be resized, nothing while it is maximized or full screen. The window buttons and the title bar's drag area inset themselves by that, so maximized they reach the window's edges and the close button takes the screen's corner, as Windows' own caption buttons do. Windowed, nothing changes.

## Test

`maximized_the_close_button_reaches_the_screens_corner` renders the custom title bar, reads the close button's clickable area windowed and maximized (the maximized one reaches further up and right), clicks the button's own corner (kittest keeps the app 8 px in from the window, so that corner stands in for the screen's): maximized it closes, windowed it does nothing, and the window's real corner still begins a resize. The test fails on main.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Say once, the first time, that closing the window keeps the launcher in the tray
author: XianZheYang
body:
For #45 and #215 (and the "it only closes from Settings → Quit" comments under them): the close button parks the launcher in the tray by design, but to someone who doesn't know that, a window that vanishes with nothing to show for it looks hung, and the reports end with killing the process.

This keeps the behaviour and the setting as they are, and adds the hint most tray apps give: **the first time** the window closes to the tray, a system notification says

> **ArtCraft Launcher is still running**
> It's in the tray: open it or quit it from the tray icon, or turn this off in the settings.

## Change

- `LauncherUi::hidden_to_tray(host)`: sends the notification through the host and records it in `Settings::tray_hint_shown`, so it happens once per install (the setting persists like the others).
- The desktop shell calls it from the close-request path only, for both ways of going to the tray (hidden where the window can hide, closed where it can't). A window hidden by clicking the tray icon, or started hidden at login, gets no hint: the user already knows about the tray there.
- Two strings, with rows in all ten complete catalogs, worded like each catalog's existing "Keep running in the tray when the window is closed".

## Test

`the_first_close_to_the_tray_is_explained_once` calls `hidden_to_tray` twice with a host that records notifications: one notification, with the expected title and a body that names the tray icon, and the setting set.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Check for updates: look past a feed that is behind GitHub
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #91: "Check for updates" didn't show a release published minutes earlier, and the reporter saw delays of 5 to 20 minutes before the launcher caught up.

## Cause

The launcher takes the ArtCraft API's feed as the answer for every app it lists and has refreshed within a day, and the feed itself polls GitHub on its own schedule. So a check the user presses right after a release gets the feed's last snapshot, however recently the feed polled, and GitHub is only asked when the feed doesn't vouch for an app. That is right for automatic checks (it is what keeps the launcher within GitHub's request limit), but a check the user presses is a question about now.

## Change

- `ReleaseSource::newest_tag(repo)`: the tag of the repo's newest stable release by a route that costs no API quota. `GitHubSource` reads it from the `releases/latest` redirect, which the quota-free fallback already uses; the default is `None`, so other sources and the test doubles are unaffected.
- `latest_for`: on a check the user pressed (`force`), and only then, before taking the feed's answer for an app it asks `newest_tag`. If that names a release newer than the feed's (or any release where the feed says there is none), the feed is treated as behind and GitHub is asked for that app, as it already is for apps the feed doesn't cover. Automatic checks are unchanged, and so is a pressed check when the redirect can't be read, fails to parse, or names nothing newer: the feed stands.

Cost: one HEAD request to github.com per app per pressed check (no API quota; the checks already run on worker threads), and one API request for an app the feed is behind on.

## Test

`refresh_asks_github_when_its_redirect_names_a_newer_release_than_the_feed`: with a source whose redirect names the feed's own release, a pressed check keeps the feed's answer and asks nothing more; when it names a newer one, the check asks GitHub and reports that release; an automatic check never probes; and an unreadable, unparsable or o…

title: Table: keep the buttons in view in narrow windows (#317)
author: atahabilder1
body:

title: Add opt-in community GitHub sources in Settings
author: LabDennis
body:
**Maintainer decision required:** this intentionally allows user-selected download/install sources outside `storytold/`, as called out by the repository's third-party-app policy. It does not bundle or recommend any third-party repository. Ownership, project history and build signatures depend on the repository each user chooses; SHA256 verification is not publisher authentication. This PR is a proposal for maintainer review, not an approval of any external app.

Adds **Settings → Sources** for public GitHub repositories and forks. title: Linux: install Craft Apps as Arch packages (pacman -U)
author: ujo4eva
body:
On Arch and the distros built on it, the launcher only offered Flatpak and the AppImage: `distro::native_package` had no answer for `ID`/`ID_LIKE` `arch`, and pacman packages could only be detected and removed, never installed or updated. This adds Arch packages as a first-class format, next to `.deb` and `.rpm`.

## What changes

- **`PackageKind::ArchPkg`** (`.pkg.tar.zst`). `distro::family` maps `arch` to it, so Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS and Omarchy (`ID_LIKE=arch`) get it ahead of Flatpak and the AppImage when pacman and its database are present. It installs with `pacman -U --noconfirm` behind the polkit prompt, through the same path as the `.deb`/`.rpm`. It's also listed in the "Install new apps as" setting, translated in every catalog.
- **The release's Arch package is named by the bundle id** (`ai.storyteller.<app>`), provides `<app>` and conflicts with `<app>`, `<app>-bin` and `<app>-git`. This is for two reasons:
  - An AUR helper treats any installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it from the AUR on the next `-Syu`.
  - The name lets the launcher tell its own package, which it updates with `pacman -U`, from an AUR build, which it still leaves to the AUR helper. That's what `is_release_arch_package` checks.
- **Repository packages.** A Craft App installed from a pacman repository (for example Omarchy's) is pointed at `sudo pacman -Syu` instead of an AUR helper. The repository is found with `pacman -Si` (`LC_ALL=C`). The new message has an `@msg` row in every catalog. The `Pacman` status label is now "Arch package" rather than "Arch package (AUR)".
- **The launcher's own release** gains `artcraft-launcher-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst`, built by nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`, through an `overrides.archlinux` block. `package.sh` renames the package to the bundle id and writes `archlinux.packager`, because nfpm doesn't env-expand that field. title: Download one app at a time, in the order they're shown
author: dquimper
body:
## Why

Installing or updating several apps at once starts every download at the same time. They share the connection, so each one crawls and none is ready soon.

## What changes

- **One download at a time.** A download requested while another is running waits. Its row shows **"Waiting for another download…"** with a cancel button.
- **Screen order, not click order.** Waiting downloads start in the order the apps are listed, following the current sort. Re-sorting while they wait changes who goes next. Apps hidden by a filter or search go after the ones on screen, in suite order. Suite order also applies until the UI has sent its first order.
- **Installing doesn't block the line.** The next download starts as soon as the previous one is downloaded and verified, while that app installs. A file already downloaded on an earlier try skips the line.
- **A "Simultaneous downloads" setting** (Settings → Updates, 1 to 4, default 1), as suggested in review. A note under it says downloads running together share the connection. It's shown only in builds that install apps. Raising it starts waiting downloads right away. Lowering it lets running downloads finish. Settings saved before this change load with 1.
- Cancelling a waiting download removes it from the line and shows "Download cancelled". The launcher's own self-update is not part of the line.

## How

- `crates/native/src/downloads.rs`: new `Downloads` queue (Mutex + Condvar, like `queue.rs`), with a guard that frees the line on drop, including on unwind. Used as `install::DOWNLOADS` around the download step in `install::install`.
- Each install takes its place in line when the backend starts the job (`Downloads::join` in `start_job`), before its thread runs. So an Update all batch goes in screen order whichever job reaches its download first. A place dropped before its turn (failed, stopped, already downloaded) leaves the line.
- `downloads.rs` counts running downloads against a limit (`set_limit`, kept between 1 and …

title: Fix Intel macOS selection of ARM-only DMGs
author: MMexicann
body:
Intel Macs currently select an ARM-only DMG when a release offers split macOS builds or only an ARM build. This can offer or install an application that the machine cannot run.

### Problem and reproduction

Construct a release containing `photocraft-0.5.0-macos-arm64.dmg` and `photocraft-0.5.0-macos-x86_64.dmg`, then call `pick_asset` with `Platform { os: MacOs, arch: X64 }` and `[Dmg]`. Main selects the ARM DMG. With only `macos-aarch64` or `macos-arm64`, it still returns that incompatible asset.

The two regression tests were added before the fix and both failed on main. The universal-build test passed.

### Root cause and implementation

`Platform::tokens` used the same macOS token list for every processor, trying ARM before Intel.

- Intel: universal, then x86_64; never ARM.
- Apple silicon: retain universal, aarch64, arm64, then the existing Intel fallback.
- Unsupported macOS architectures: no compatible token.

The production change is confined to this token match and its documentation. There are no dependency, packaging, UI, or localization changes.

### Automated coverage and verification

Four tests cover split builds, refusal of both ARM spellings on Intel, universal preference even when split builds are listed first, Apple silicon's ARM support and Intel fallback, and unsupported architecture rejection. Universal selection uses a trimmed real [PhotoCraft v0.9.0 release](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/releases/tag/v0.9.0) JSON fixture.

- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-core macos` before the fix: two regressions failed; universal selection passed.
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-core` after the fix: **35 passed, 1 existing test ignored**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: **all four steps passed** — formatting, workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests (**285 passed, 2 existing tests ignored**), and Wasm checks.
- `cargo xtask wasm`: **passed** for core and the web app.

Validation ran on Windows x64 GNU with Rust…

title: Fix XDG autostart command quoting
author: IanHollow
body:
Autostart currently escapes only double quotes in the executable path. Paths containing backslashes, dollar signs, backticks or percent signs can produce an incorrect Desktop Entry Exec argument.

Reuse the existing Desktop Entry quoting function in a pure autostart renderer. Reject control characters and non-UTF-8 paths before writing the entry. Keep the ArtCraft Launcher identity and --hidden argument unchanged.

The proposed regressions cover special-character and Unicode paths, the hidden flag and identity fields, and rejected paths. Linux and FreeBSD use this renderer; macOS and Windows retain their existing login mechanisms.

Validation: Rustfmt 1.98.1 passed with the project formatting settings. Compilation, focused Cargo tests, Clippy and `cargo xtask ci` have not run for this proposal. Prior downstream package builds do not validate this upstream patch.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex (GPT-6). The contributor has reviewed this PR. The deferred checks listed above remain required before merge.

title: Match portable delta entries by relative path under renamed top folders
author: PanDuroDev
body:
Stacked on #345 - please review only the last commit here (`51bfdca`); everything below it is #345. This will be rebased onto main the moment #345 merges. Closes #423.

Problem (#423): every portable entry path embeds the version (`photocraft-0.8.2-.../photocraft.exe` vs `photocraft-0.9.0-...`), so the exact-name matcher finds zero common names out of 9 plus 9 in the real zips and the delta always falls back to a full download. Verified against the published zips (downloaded, compared locally, no repo changes).

Change: `plan()` compares paths relative to each directory own single top folder when both sides have exactly one (backslashes normalized); anything ambiguous (flat names, several tops, strays) keeps the exact-name behavior byte-identically. Copy still requires method plus CRC32 plus compressed size, and validation, the local-header cross-check and the final SHA-256 are untouched. A log line records when relative matching applies.

Safety: the single production caller of `plan()` is the portable-zip delta; unpacking always uses the new full names, so stripping only ever affects the copy/fetch decision, and the worst case is today behavior (full download).

Tests: `common_top` matrix (one/flat/multi tops, backslash, top-dir entries, empty), `plan` across renamed tops, and a new end-to-end delta test with `v1/` vs `v2/` tops proving partial reuse. Gates green: fmt, clippy with -D warnings, core 40 plus native 114 plus zip-delta integration 5.

Honest limit: field proof of partial reuse across versions needs a future release pair with shared content; the 0.8.2 to 0.9.0 pair shares nothing by name even relatively (verified), so it would still download fully - correctly.

_Note: drafted with AI assistance (Muse Spark)._

title: Chinese: look for a hand-installed MiSans too, in the user's font folders
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #378: a system whose only Chinese face is MiSans (Xiaomi's free font, installed by hand) got

```
WARN artcraft_launcher_ui_egui::cjk_font] no Chinese font found on this system (looked for PingFang SC, Hiragino Sans GB, Heiti SC, Microsoft YaHei, SimSun, Noto Sans CJK SC and WenQuanYi)
```

and an interface that stayed in English.

## Change

`chinese_candidates` now ends with MiSans (`MiSans-Regular.ttf`, then `-Normal`, then `-Medium`; the family name in the files is `MiSans`, which `face_index` matches), looked for where hand-installed fonts go:

- macOS: `~/Library/Fonts`, `/Library/Fonts`
- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` (where "Install for me", the default since 1809, puts fonts), then `%SystemRoot%\Fonts`
- Linux and the BSDs: `~/.local/share/fonts` (and its `MiSans`/`misans` subfolders), `~/.fonts`, and the usual packaged places (`/usr/share/fonts/{MiSans,misans,TTF}`, `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/misans`, `/usr/local/share/fonts/MiSans`)

It comes after the system's own faces, which are complete families with hinting the system tuned. The "none found" log line names it.

title: Details: a page just opened starts at the top
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #428: scroll down an app's details page, open another app's page, and it came up scrolled to the same place instead of at the top.

## Cause

One `ScrollArea` serves every app's page in the drawer, and egui keeps a scroll area's offset by its id, so the next page inherited the last one's offset.

## Change

The drawer already notes the frame it opens on an app (where it resets the picture index and the enlarged view). It now also sets `detail_scroll_top`, and on that frame the scroll area is shown with `vertical_scroll_offset(0.0)`. Reopening the same app starts at the top too.

## Test

`an_apps_page_opens_at_the_top_however_far_the_last_one_was_scrolled` opens PhotoCraft's page, scrolls it well down with the wheel, closes it with Esc, opens VectorCraft's and checks its links sit where PhotoCraft's did before scrolling. On main it fails with the page opened 891 px further down.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Update dialog: ask about downloading, not relaunching, where the copy can't update itself
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #388.

The "ArtCraft Launcher {version} is available." dialog had one line of text whichever button it showed: "A new version is available. Would you like to relaunch with the updated version?". That fits **Update and restart**. A copy that can't replace itself (`Capabilities::self_update` false: a sandboxed copy, a tarball, the web build, FreeBSD) gets **Download** instead, which opens the release in the browser and closes the dialog; nothing relaunches.

## Change

Such a copy now asks "A new version is available. Download it to replace this version?". The sentence is chosen in `launcher_update_dialog` from the same capability that chooses the button. Rows in all ten complete catalogs; the i18n completeness test passes.

## Test

`a_copy_that_cannot_update_itself_is_asked_about_downloading_not_relaunching` runs the harness without self-update and checks the dialog shows the new question, not the relaunch one, offers no "Update and restart", and that Download opens the release's file.

title: Windows: draw on the GPU Windows' Graphics setting names for the launcher
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #399: on a hybrid laptop the launcher kept the discrete NVIDIA GPU awake (about 8 W at idle in the report) even though Windows' Graphics settings said **Power saving** for the launcher's exe.

## Cause

On Windows the launcher picks its adapter itself (`wgpu_options`, so that Direct3D 12 and WARP come before GL), and `adapter_rank` puts the discrete GPU first unless wgpu's power preference is `LowPower`, which only `WGPU_POWER_PREF` ever sets. The choice Windows records for the exe was never consulted.

## Change

- `artcraft_launcher_native::graphics::windows_gpu_preference()` reads that choice: Settings stores it under `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\DirectX\UserGpuPreferences`, one value per exe path, as `GpuPreference=1;` (power saving) or `GpuPreference=2;` (high performance); `None` for "Let Windows decide" or an exe nothing was recorded for. The parsing is a pure function with tests; the registry read uses `winreg`, already a dependency.
- `prefer_integrated` in the desktop shell decides the order: `WGPU_POWER_PREF` if set (a developer's override, as on Linux), else Windows' choice for the exe, else wgpu's default preference as before. So nothing changes for anyone who hasn't set anything, and "Power saving" now does what it says.

The safe fallback stays: an integrated GPU with no Direct3D 12 driver still loses to WARP, and WARP to any hardware D3D12 adapter, as before.

## Tests

`windows_graphics_setting_picks_the_gpu_unless_the_environment_does` covers each combination; `reads_windows_gpu_preference_values` covers the value format, including "Let Windows decide" and junk. I can't exercise the registry read itself from here (no Windows machine), but it is the same `winreg` call `self_update` already makes for `InstallDir`.

`cargo xtask ci`'s steps pass locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm); the native crate's tests were run serially, as its macOS-only disk-image test is flaky in parallel on this machine (a separate PR makes it retry).

title: Tests: retry hdiutil create in the macOS checks, and say what it said
author: XianZheYang
body:
Test reliability on macOS: `install::tests::macos_checks::the_bundle_must_be_the_releases_version` fails now and then with nothing more than

```
hdiutil create failed
```

In runs of `cargo xtask ci` on an M-series Mac today it failed in 4 of 7 full runs and 1 of 3 runs of the `macos_checks` tests alone; alone, the test always passes. The helper that builds the test's disk images already holds `macos::DISK_IMAGES` so the tests' own `hdiutil` calls don't overlap, but the disk-image helper turns a `create` away while it is busy with anything else on the machine, which is why `attach` in the production code retries it (#135).

## Change

The test helper `dmg` now tries `hdiutil create` up to five times with a short, growing pause, and keeps hdiutil's stderr for the failure message, so a real failure says why rather than just that it happened. Test code only; no change to the launcher.

With this, 10 consecutive runs of the `macos_checks` tests passed here.

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a dialog in the launcher — the family's hub. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the dialog says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **The hub's tasks** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside the ArtCraft Launcher and names the whole family — GridCraft spreadsheets, WordCraft documents, DeckCraft presentations, SoundCraft audio, CADCraft drafting, LightCraft photos, FilmCraft video, EffectCraft motion, PhotoCraft image editing, PDFCraft PDFs, DesignCraft layout, VectorCraft vector art, ArtCraft generative creation — so "which app for this?" gets a real answer. The honesty clause: never invent app or version names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

title: fix(install): menu entries list the file types each app opens
author: mflkee
body:
An AppImage install writes `<data>/applications/ai.storyteller.<app>.desktop` without `MimeType=`, so the desktop has no way to offer the app for a file: a fresh GridCraft install never opens an `.xlsx` from the file manager or "Open with", and no default can be pointed at it.

The launcher's own AppRun and PhotoCraft's already call `update-desktop-database` for the same reason.

title: fix(install): reclaim menu entries left dangling by an upgrade
author: bowfeng
body:
## What was happening

After an update, **10 of the 12 craft apps vanished from the app menu** on a
real Linux box. Repro shape on disk (what an update leaves behind):

```
[Desktop Entry]
Name=CADCraft
Exec=/home/…/.local/bin/cadcraft %F            # a wrapper, still works
TryExec=/home/…/Applications/cadcraft-0.6.2-…AppImage   # removed by the update
```

The launcher only replaces/removes a menu entry it itself wrote (the
`X-ArtCraft-Launcher=true` marker) or one that runs a copy it just replaced.
The old unmarked entries were shipped by the apps' own `AppRun`, so on upgrade
`integrate_into()` logged `leaving the existing menu entry … alone`. The update
then deleted the old AppImage, leaving `TryExec` pointing at a file that no
longer exists — and **GNOME hides the whole app for such an entry**. With the
entry neither ours nor pointing at the new copy, no later install or uninstall
would ever touch it again: the app was gone for good.

## Fix

`integrate_into()` now also replaces an entry whose `Exec=`/`TryExec=` names an
**absolute path that no longer exists** (new `desktop_entry::is_dangling()`).
Such an entry is already invisible to the user, so taking it over and marking it
is strictly better than leaving it. Entries that still point at a live file, and
bare command names resolved from `$PATH` (not file references), are left alone
as before — the "only touch our own entries" guarantee is preserved for every
entry that still works.

## Tests

- `desktop_entry::tests::dangling_detection_matches_what_the_upgrade_leaves_behind`
  — the real-world entry shape, plus quoted-path / bare-name / live-file /
  own-entry cases.
- `install::tests::adds_and_removes_only_its_own_menu_entry_and_icon` — new
  regression case: a dangling unmarked entry is reclaimed; the existing
  "someone else's live entry is left alone" assertion kept (re-pointed at
  `/bin/sh`, which exists, so it stays a genuinely-live foreign entry).

title: fix(ui): ask wgpu for no more than the GPU offers
author: nictoumayan
body:
## Problem

On a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 (V3D 7.1.10.2, Mesa 26.2.2 V3DV, labwc on Wayland) the launcher exits before its first frame:

```
ERROR eframe::native::run] Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Limit 'max_inter_stage_shader_variables' value 16 is better than allowed 15
```

eframe 0.36's default `device_descriptor` asks for `wgpu::Limits::default()` on every backend but GL (`downlevel_webgl2_defaults()` on GL), each with `max_texture_dimension_2d: 8192`, and never compares it with the adapter. V3DV reports `maxVertexOutputComponents` = 64, so wgpu allows 15 inter-stage variables, and its 2D textures stop at 7680 (4096 through GL). `request_device` fails on the first limit the adapter can't meet, and the launcher quits.

## Fix

`within_adapter_limits` wraps egui's descriptor and lowers each requested limit to the adapter's where the adapter offers less (`Limits::or_worse_values_from`). egui's shaders use two inter-stage variables, so nothing it draws needs the defaults. GPUs that meet the defaults get the same request as before. It applies on every platform, since any GPU short of a default limit fails the same way.

## Testing

- On the CM5 the launcher now opens and stays up, started both from a terminal and from a desktop entry.
- `the_device_asks_for_no_more_than_the_gpu_offers` checks the V3D limit and that a GPU offering more still gets egui's request.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

The Craft Apps have the same bug in their own code: storytold/lightcraft#862, storytold/vectorcraft#2105, storytold/pdfcraft#2383, storytold/photocraft#5986.

title: Keep Nix-managed bundles and launcher updates under Nix control
author: IanHollow
body:
A Craft app installed by Nix can appear in the macOS Applications folder through a symlink. ArtCraft Launcher recognizes the bundle, but currently treats it like a manually installed copy that it may replace or remove. The same bundle detection can offer self-update for a Nix-installed launcher.

This keeps those copies under Nix's control. Before updating or removing an app, the backend resolves its location and refuses changes to an output in the conventional `/nix/store`. A launcher running from that store does not offer self-update. Opening an app and reading its installed version keep their existing behavior.

This does not change discovery order, introduce a Nix package format, or change AppImage integration. Custom Nix store locations are outside this fix. Linux PATH installations already use the existing externally managed binary handling; the new guard also protects bundle and launcher records whose targets belong to Nix.

Related to #328's Nix runtime support and #373's externally managed Windows copies, with a separate macOS ownership case.

Validation:

- Formatting passes. The change adds no dependency or serialized source type.
- Two standalone tests of the extracted final ownership helper passed, covering absolute/store boundaries, missing-path escapes and temporary executable/profile/bundle symlinks, including ordinary links outside the store.
- A separate source-extracted ownership regression failed on current main and passed after the change. Its ordinary-app and AUR policy checks passed before and after. These focused checks use minimal type shims and do not replace native crate CI.
- The committed native regression invokes the real install and uninstall entry points and checks refusal before download validation or installer phases. This test has not yet been compiled or run.
- Native workspace CI and macOS runtime verification remain pending. No full application build was run.

title: feat(install): choose where Craft apps are installed
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

Craft apps always install to the system location: Program Files, `/Applications`, or `~/Applications`. People with a small system drive or a dedicated apps folder can't change that. This is the most requested install feature (#157, #93, #74, #76). It's a smaller take on #227.

## What changes for users

- **Settings › Default install folder.** Type a path or use Browse…. Use default goes back to the system location.
- **Installing an app asks for its folder.** The field is prefilled with the default and can be changed for that app alone. The choice is remembered per app.
- **Updates stay where the app already is.** A new folder only affects new installs.
- **Flatpak and web builds** keep the system location and skip the prompt.

## How

- `InstallLocations { root, per_app }` lives in `Settings` and is sent to the backend inside `BackendOptions`. `folder(app)` gives the per-app folder, else the default.
- `install::destination` chooses the folder. An update goes beside the launcher's own copy. A new install goes to the chosen folder, which must exist and be writable, else the platform default.
- **Windows.** The MSI gets `INSTALLFOLDER="<folder>\<App>"`, the property the Craft apps' WiX files use. The MSI saves that folder as `HKLM\Software\<App>\InstallDir` for its upgrades. Detection now falls back to that value, so Open finds the exe.
- **macOS.** The `.app` is copied into the folder. DMG installs now save a record, and detection reads the bundle at the recorded path. Uninstall now fails instead of permanently deleting the app when it can't be moved to Trash, which happens across volumes.
- **Linux.** A custom folder installs the AppImage, with desktop integration pointing at it. An existing file the launcher didn't install is never overwritten.
- The folder picker is `rfd` with the XDG portal backend, so there is no GTK dependency.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` pass on Linux. Clippy also passes…

title: fix(windows): don't start wgpu's GL backend when Direct3D 12 has an adapter
author: nanderq
body:
## Problem

On a hybrid-GPU Windows laptop (NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop + AMD Radeon iGPU on the Oct 2022 OEM driver, plus two DisplayLink adapters) the launcher exits before any window appears, on every launch:

```
Faulting module name: atio6axx.dll, version: 31.0.12044.3
Exception code: 0xc0000005
Fault offset: 0x0000000000131cc2
```

On Windows the launcher asks wgpu for `DX12 | GL`. While wgpu enumerates adapters, its GL backend makes a WGL context, which loads every GPU's OpenGL driver, and AMD's old `atio6axx.dll` crashes inside it. Direct3D 12 draws fine on this machine (`WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` works around it), and it reproduces on `main` (0.4.1) as well as v0.3.2.

## Fix

`dx12_has_adapter` asks a Direct3D 12-only wgpu instance for its adapters once, before eframe makes its own. If Direct3D 12 lists one, the backends are `DX12` alone and the GL backend never starts. GL is added only when Direct3D 12 lists nothing. Windows 10 and later always have WARP, so in practice that only happens where Direct3D 12 itself is missing or broken. `WGPU_BACKEND` still overrides the default, and `adapter_rank` still puts any Direct3D 12 adapter before GL. Vulkan stays out for the reason already documented (`amdvlk64.dll` crashes on hybrid AMD laptops).

`pollster` (Windows only, already in `Cargo.lock` through eframe) waits on wgpu's adapter list.

## Testing

- On the laptop above, with `WGPU_BACKEND` removed from the environment, the launcher opens the ArtCraft Launcher window and stays up. `atio6axx.dll` is no longer loaded into the process (`d3d12.dll` is), and the Application log shows no new crash.
- The GL fallback itself isn't exercised: Direct3D 12 always lists an adapter on this machine.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Reject corrupt and future self-update timestamps
author: MMexicann
body:
A corrupt self-update marker can panic while checking for launcher updates, and a future timestamp can suppress an update beyond the intended 24-hour grace period.

### Reproduction and root cause

Write the release tag and `-9223372036854775808` on the two lines of `<data>/self-update.txt`, then check that same release with `just_updated_to`. The unchecked `now - at` subtraction overflows. A future timestamp also satisfies the old `age < 24h` condition because negative ages were accepted.

### Implementation and coverage

Use checked subtraction and require an age in `0..24h`. Invalid or future markers no longer suppress updates. The existing grace period for a genuinely recent matching release is preserved. The production change is one line, with no new dependencies or user-facing strings.

Two regression tests use temporary marker files: the minimum signed timestamp reproduces the overflow; a day-ahead timestamp and `i64::MAX` reproduce incorrect suppression. The existing tests retain coverage for recent markers, other release tags, and expiry.

- Before the fix, `cargo test --workspace self_update_timestamp` failed both new tests: arithmetic overflow and incorrect acceptance of a future timestamp.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: **all four steps passed** — formatting, workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests (**285 passed, 2 existing ignored**), and core/web Wasm checks.
- Both new timestamp regressions passed in the full suite.

### Platforms and safety

Validation runs on Windows x64 GNU with Rust 1.99.0, using workspace TEMP/TMP and disabling incremental compilation for sandbox filesystem restrictions. Linux, macOS and FreeBSD runtime execution are not available locally. No real installation or privileged installer is used. Packaging is unchanged, so shellcheck/actionlint and packaging validation are not applicable.

title: Stop download retry loops when a partial file cannot be removed
author: MMexicann
body:
An oversized cached partial download can leave its worker spinning until the user cancels if the partial file cannot be removed, for example while another process holds a Windows file lock.

### Reproduction and root cause

Create a `.part` file larger than the expected release size, then hold it open without delete sharing on Windows. `fetch_resuming` sees the oversized file, ignores the removal error, and immediately repeats with the same file size. No download attempt can make progress. A directory at the partial-file path exercises the same failed removal on Unix.

### Implementation and tests

Propagate the removal failure through the existing download file error format. The user receives the filesystem error instead of an endless local retry loop. The blocked file remains intact, and a later retry can recover after the lock or filesystem problem is resolved. This changes one production line.

Two tests use temporary files and a loopback HTTP server:
- An ordinary oversized partial is removed, the download restarts from byte zero, and the published SHA-256 is verified.
- A partial that cannot be removed returns a file error and remains intact. The Windows fixture uses an owned file handle; the Unix fixture uses a directory. A cancellation watchdog bounds the old loop so the regression cannot hang the suite.

Before the fix, `cargo test --workspace oversized_partial` produced **1 passed, 1 failed**: normal recovery passed, while the blocked-file case returned `cancelled` only after the watchdog stopped its loop. `git diff --check` passed. `cargo xtask ci`: **all four steps passed** — formatting, workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests (**285 passed, 2 existing ignored**), and core/web Wasm checks. Both new download regressions passed, including the Windows file-lock case.

author: FredApps
body:

title: macOS: build again after install_dmg gained a replace argument
author: dquimper
body:
## Problem

`main` (since #461, `307efcf`) no longer compiles on macOS:

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 7 arguments but 6 arguments were supplied
   --> crates/native/src/self_update.rs:184:26
    |     install::macos::install_dmg(&LAUNCHER, &file, Some(&existing), None, paths, &…)
    |                                                                         ----- argument #5 of type `bool` is missing
```

#461 added a `replace: bool` argument to `install::macos::install_dmg`, but the two calls in `self_update.rs` weren't updated: the macOS self-update (line 184) and the `the_new_bundle_replaces_the_running_one` test (line 374). `main`'s CI passed, which suggests per-PR CI doesn't build the macOS target.

## Fix

Pass `replace: true` in both calls. The bundle being replaced is the running launcher itself, so self-update writes over it unconditionally, which is how it behaved before #461. With `false`, self-update would depend on the new "already exists and wasn't installed by ArtCraft Launcher" check recognising the launcher's own bundle.

## Testing (macOS arm64)

- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt and clippy pass, and wasm passes.
- `self_update::tests::the_new_bundle_replaces_the_running_one` passes.
- `install::tests::macos_checks::*` are intermittently flaky on this machine with `hdiutil: attach failed - Resource temporarily unavailable` (disk-image mounting contention, not this change; #289 reports the same on unmodified `main`). They pass on rerun: 2 of 3 serial runs passed fully.

author: GabrielMatozo
body:
Fixes #462

## What was wrong

`README.md`, "Build from source", linked the bundler as `[trunk](https://trunkrs.dev/)`. That domain no longer serves the bundler: it was re-registered and now serves an unrelated site.

Wayback snapshots of `https://trunkrs.dev/`:

| Snapshot | Content |
|---|---|
| 2026-04-01 | `Trunk \| Efficient Web Application Bundler for Rust with Minimal Configuration` |
| 2026-08-24 | unrelated site |
| 2026-10-01 | unrelated site |

## Why not `trunk.dev` as the issue proposed

`https://trunk.dev/` resolves to HTTP 200, but it is a different product: `Trunk — Agent-scale version control` (Balearic Labs LLC), not the Rust/WAsm bundler. Pointing the README there would swap one wrong link for another.

The bundler's own repo is the source of truth for its site:

- `trunk-rs/trunk` README: *"Head on over to the [Trunk website](https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk)"*
- `trunk-rs/trunk` `site/config.toml`: `base_url = "https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/"`

So this PR uses `https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/`.

## Change

One line in `README.md`:

```diff
-The web version builds with [trunk](https://trunkrs.dev/):
+The web version builds with [trunk](https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/):
```

A repo-wide search found no other occurrence of the old URL. Docs-only change, so `cargo xtask ci` is unaffected.
