title: macOS: skip wgpu's indirect-call validation on Intel Macs
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Fixes #344, fixes #516, fixes #561.

On Intel Iris and Iris Pro Macs the launcher exits at startup. Metal's compiler fails on wgpu's indirect-validation compute shader (`wgpu_core::indirect_validation ... Compiler encountered an internal error`), the device is lost, and eframe exits with `WGPU error: Parent device is lost`.

## Cause

egui-wgpu's default instance flags are `InstanceFlags::from_build_config().with_env()`, which in wgpu 30 include `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL`, so `request_device` compiles the validation shaders. The macOS `wgpu_options()` returned that default unchanged.

## Fix

On x86_64 macOS builds, `wgpu_options()` removes `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` and then applies `with_env()`, so `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` still turns it on. The launcher issues no indirect draws or dispatches. Apple silicon, Windows and Linux keep wgpu's default. This copies PhotoCraft's fix and its `skips_indirect_validation` helper (storytold/photocraft#3171, `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`).

No Intel Mac was available here. In #561, pauerbuk reported that `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=0` makes 0.4.1 start and work on an Intel Iris Mac mini; this change makes that the default. Thanks to pauerbuk for the workaround.

#514 has no log and stays open. #38 (`metal3.2` on OpenCore Legacy Patcher systems) is a different fault and stays open.

## Tests

- `intel_macs_skip_the_indirect_validation_shaders`: the helper returns true for an Intel Mac and false for Apple silicon, Windows, Linux and FreeBSD.
- `intel_macs_create_the_device_without_indirect_validation` (macOS): on x86_64, `wgpu_options()` lacks the flag unless `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` turns it on; on Apple silicon it keeps wgpu's flags. Built for x86_64 and run under Rosetta (`cargo test -p artcraft-launcher --target x86_64-apple-darwin`), it fails on `main` with `InstanceFlags(DEBUG | VALIDATION | VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL)` and passes with the change, with the variable unset, `1` and `0`.

title: Don't offer Resume for a download that never connected
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #576.

`start_job` rewrites every `PAUSED` the user didn't ask for into *"The download paused because the connection keeps dropping. Press Resume to continue where it stopped."*, whether or not any bytes arrived.

When nothing arrived:

- there is no part file, so `report_partial` emits `Event::Paused { download: None }` and the card shows the plain **Install** button. The text named a Resume control that isn't on screen.
- "the connection keeps dropping" describes a connection that was never made.

## The change

`start_job` now asks the same question `report_partial` does — does a part file hold any bytes? — and picks the text to match:

- **bytes on disk** → unchanged wording, Resume really is there;
- **nothing on disk** → *"The download didn't start: nothing could be reached, so there is nothing to resume. Check your connection and try again."*

The choice moved into `paused_message(resumable: bool)` so it can be tested on its own.

## Verified on Windows

ArtCraft Launcher built from this branch, Windows 11 Pro 25H2, run in portable mode so the test used its own data folder.

1. Start once with a network so the release cache fills.
2. Restart with `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9` and `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9` (nothing listens on port 9).
3. Press Install on FigCraft 0.7.0, keep the default folder.

The log shows the retries ending as the issue describes:

```
figcraft-0.7.0-windows-x64.msi: couldn't connect: io: ... (os error 10061); retrying   [x8]
figcraft-0.7.0-windows-x64.msi: no progress after 8 attempts; pausing
```

No `.part` file exists anywhere under the data folder afterwards, so `partial_bytes` returns `None` and the new branch is the one taken. The toast now reads *"The download didn't start: nothing could be reached…"*, and the card returns to **Install**, which is consistent: there is no Resume button, and the text no longer claims one.

title: fix(notes): draw the markup in release notes instead of its markers (#591)
author: GabrielMatozo
body:
Closes #591.

## What was wrong

`draw()` classified a line as heading, bullet or text and then painted the whole line in one
`ui.label`, so every inline marker reached the screen as typed. The screenshot in the issue shows
exactly that: a file reference drawn as `From [`docs/scorecard.md`](https://github.com/…) (done /
partial / missing):` — backticks and brackets as characters, the URL wrapped mid-path because it
was plain text — and bullets reading `**Tools:** 29 / 13 / 1`.

## What this does

- `spans()` splits a line into its inline pieces (`Plain`, `Bold`, `Code`, `Link`), and `inline()`
  draws them: bold in Inter 600, code in Geist Mono, and a link as a hyperlink carrying its own
  label, so the URL no longer has to be read — or wrapped — inside the note.
- A heading draws no emphasis, so it gets its text with the markers dropped.
- A link is clickable only when `core::release::safe_web_link` accepts it, exactly like the
  pull-request link beside it; otherwise its label is drawn as plain text. A release body is
  hostile input.
- Only the markup a release body actually carries is recognised. A lone `*`, a marker pair with a
  space inside it, an unclosed marker and `[text](url "title")` all stay literal, so text such as
  `29 * 3` or `snake_case_name` keeps every character.
- A line with no markup keeps the single label it had, so the fold ("Show N more changes"), the
  dialog's own zoom and every other line are untouched.

Nested emphasis is the one thing left half-rendered: `***x***` draws the inner run and leaves the
outer asterisks visible, rather than growing a full inline-markdown engine. No character is dropped.

## Two things the first draft got wrong

- The link search runs again after every unmatched `[`, so searching to the end of the line cost a
  scan per bracket: **1.07 s on a 64 KiB line of `[`**, the `release::MAX_NOTES` ceiling, and a line
  is parsed twice per frame. The label and address searches now stay inside a small window — a link
  …

title: Survive a lost graphics device: open a new window instead of crashing (#274)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #274.

## Cause

The launcher's window draws with a wgpu device. A driver reset can lose that device: for example when the PC wakes from sleep, the GPU driver recovers from a hang, or the OS kills a long submission. The launcher never handled that:
- **egui-wgpu panics** on the next frame with shapes, in `renderer.rs:984`: "Failed to create staging buffer for index data". That's this issue's message.
- **wgpu's default uncaptured-error handler panics too**, on the errors that follow a loss.

PhotoCraft had the same crash (storytold/photocraft#1215, fixed in storytold/photocraft#6464). The launcher can do better than PhotoCraft does, though: it already reopens its window in a loop for the tray, and each new window gets a fresh device.

## Change

- **New `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/gpu_health.rs`, with `WindowGpu`:**
  - `set_device_lost_callback` records the loss.
  - `on_uncaptured_error` logs errors instead of panicking.
  - `lost()` polls the device once per frame, without blocking. `Device::poll` panics on a lost device, so the poll is guarded with `catch_unwind`, and a panic there counts as a loss.
- **`Shell::ui`:** once the device is lost, the frame draws nothing (`ctx.graphics_mut` is cleared), so egui-wgpu has nothing to upload. The shell sets `Launcher::reopen_window` (keeping the window hidden if it was) and closes the window. The close handler doesn't treat that close as "go to the tray".
- **The window loop in `main`:** when `reopen_window` is set, the next `run_native` pass starts straight away, with a new window and a new device. `ReopenBudget` allows that at most 3 times in 10 minutes, so a GPU that keeps failing can't open windows in a loop. Past the budget, the launcher carries on in the tray (or exits where there's no tray), as when the window is closed.
- **Strings:** no new user-facing text; only log lines.

## Tests

- **`gpu_health::tests::a_destroyed_device_reads_as_lost_without_panicking`:** `Device::destroy()` then reads as lost, and …

title: fix(windows): repoint the start-at-login entry when the launcher has moved (#595)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #595.

On Windows, start at login is a `HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run` value that stores the launcher's full exe path. `is_enabled` only checks that the value exists, so after the launcher is reinstalled or moved to another folder the toggle still shows "on" while the value points at an exe that is no longer there. That matches the report: Task Manager lists the entry, "Open file location" is greyed out, nothing starts at login, and turning the option off and on again fixes it (the toggle rewrites the value with the current path).

Changes:
- `login::refresh()`, called once at startup in the primary instance: if the `Run` value exists and differs from what this exe would write, it rewrites the value through `set_enabled(true)` and logs the old and new value. If start at login is off, nothing changes.
- `run_value(exe)` builds the value in one place, shared by `set_enabled` and `refresh`. `repointed(stored, exe)` decides whether a rewrite is needed.
- Windows only, because the report is about Windows. macOS and Linux `set_enabled` paths are unchanged.

The repaired entry takes effect from the next login after the launcher has been opened once (for example from the Start menu), since a stale entry can't start the launcher itself.

Tests: `run_value_quotes_the_path_and_starts_hidden` checks the value format, and `a_run_value_for_an_old_location_is_repointed_at_this_one` checks that a value for another path gets rewritten and the current one is left alone.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * The launcher now checks its Windows startup entry whenever it starts as the primary instance. If the entry points to a program that no longer exists, it is updated to the current launcher location. Valid entries are left unchanged, and the launcher continues to start hidden. This helps keep automatic startup working after the launcher is moved or updated.

title: feat(install): app/system default in the Install dialog, free-space warning, install location in details
author: Belligerently
body:
## What this does

Three related improvements to installing apps, all in the Install dialog and the details drawer.

**1. The Install dialog offers the app default, the system default, or a custom folder.**
Today, once a default folder is set in Settings, the dialog has no way to put one app back in the
system's usual place: "Use default" means the launcher's default. The dialog now shows three choices
(`widgets::cells`, like the theme picker):

- **App default**: the folder from Settings, shown by name (or "same as the system default" when none is set)
- **System default**: the system's usual place, even when Settings has a default folder
- **Custom folder**: the folder field and Browse…, plus "Make this my default install folder"

`InstallLocations` gains a `system` set for apps that keep the system's place; `folder()` returns
`None` for them. It is `#[serde(default)]`, so existing settings load unchanged. The dialog opens on
whatever the app used last. When a translation is too wide for one row, the options stack.

**2. Free space on the target drive.**
The dialog shows how much room the drive under the chosen folder has, and warns (without blocking)
when there is less than about twice the download. That's roughly enough room to download and then
unpack. A folder that doesn't exist yet is measured at its nearest existing parent. This goes through a new
`Host::free_space` (default `None`, so the web build shows nothing) and
`native::paths::free_space`, which uses `fs4` (MIT OR Apache-2.0) so the native crate stays free of
`unsafe`.

**3. Where an installed app lives.**
An installed app's details drawer gets an "Installed at" box with the path (selectable) and the
existing Show in Finder/Explorer action (`Command::Reveal`).

title: feat: add support for updating third-party apps
author: MegaTheLEGEND

# Add support for third-party apps

## Summary

This PR introduces a feature that may be somewhat controversial: support for third-party applications in Craft Launcher.

Many AI reimplementation projects have similar or identical release-page structures, making them good candidates for integration into Craft Launcher.

Third-party app support is **disabled by default**. Users must explicitly enable the feature by navigating to **Settings > Third-Party Apps > Add App** and configuring an application. Until a user does this, the feature remains completely inactive.

**ArtCraft does not provide support for third-party applications.** The UI makes this distinction clear, informing users that external applications are not officially supported by ArtCraft and that responsibility for their maintenance and functionality lies with their respective developers.

### Changes
- Add a custom app system for defining and managing third-party applications.
- Keep third-party app functionality disabled until a user explicitly configures an app.
- Integrate third-party apps into the catalog, detection, installation, and uninstallation workflows.
- Extend the native backend and application protocol to support the new functionality.
- Add settings, dialogs, and views for configuring and managing third-party apps.
- Clearly communicate the third-party support disclaimer in the UI.
- Add translations for the new UI strings across supported locales.
- Update documentation to reflect the new functionality and support boundaries.

The goal is to make third-party applications available to users who explicitly choose to configure them, while preserving the default experience and maintaining a clear distinction between ArtCraft-supported applications and externally maintained projects.

title: portable: install a ZIP that wraps its program in one folder
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2461, where a portable install fails with

> The portable ZIP does not contain the expected executable at its root.

## Cause

`crates/native/src/portable.rs` looks for the executable only at the ZIP root:

```rust
.find(|relative| {
    relative.parent().is_some_and(|p| p.as_os_str().is_empty())
        && relative.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str())
            .is_some_and(|name| app.stems().any(|stem| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&format!("{stem}.exe"))))
})
.ok_or("The portable ZIP does not contain the expected executable at its root.")?
```

A release ZIP almost always wraps everything in one folder — `VectorCraft-1.2.3/vectorcraft.exe` — and those are refused outright.

Searching deeper would not have been enough on its own. Every entry is installed at the path it carries in the ZIP (`destination.join(relative)`, read back from `unpacked.join(relative)`), so the wrapper folder would have been installed too and the program would have landed one level down.

## Change

One wrapping folder is dropped — from the folder the files are read from *and* from the names they are installed under — so a wrapped ZIP installs exactly as one packed flat does. The existing root-level search then works unchanged.

Only when it is unambiguous:

| ZIP | result |
|---|---|
| `App-1.2.3/app.exe`, `App-1.2.3/data/fonts.bin` | wrapper dropped |
| `app.exe`, `data/fonts.bin` | left alone — already flat |
| `App/app.exe`, `README.txt` | left alone — stripping would lose the file beside it |
| `a/app.exe`, `b/fonts.bin` | left alone — nothing unambiguous to strip |

Only the outermost folder goes; a deeper tree keeps its shape.

## Where it lives, and why

The decision is pure path reasoning, so it is in a new `portable_layout` module that is **not** gated, rather than inside `portable`, which `lib.rs` declares `#[cfg(windows)]`. `portable` calls it in one line:

```rust
let (unpacked, files) = crate::portable_layout::unwrap_single_folder(unpacked, files);
```

T…

title: An icon at the start of every menu row
author: EternalShade3D
body:
## What

Every row of an app's `...` menu now starts with a small icon:

| Row | Icon |
| --- | --- |
| Release notes | `file-text` |
| Download again, and each per-platform download | `download` |
| Open | `play` |
| Show in Explorer / Reveal in Finder / Open containing folder | `folder-open` |
| Reinstall | `rotate-ccw` |
| Uninstall… | `trash-2`, tinted the theme's red |
| Website | `globe` (already in the repo) |
| GitHub repository | `github` (already in the repo) |
| All releases | `tag` |
| Hide App / Unhide App | `eye-off` / `eye` |

## Why

The menu is a column of similar-looking words, and the two that remove something sit next to the
ones that only open a page. A shape at the start of each row makes the list readable at a glance
and gives Uninstall a colour of its own.

## How

- New `widgets::menu_item()` draws the icon, then the label, inside a row that is exactly as wide
  as its longest label, with a hover that runs to the edge of the menu. A translated label can be
  much longer than the English it was written from, and a row narrower than its label cannot be
  clicked.
- It reports only the label to the accessibility tree, so anything finding a row by name still
  finds it, and screen readers do not have to describe decoration.
- Icons are [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) 0.468.0, ISC, on their own 24 px grid, in `assets/icons/`,
  with `stroke` set to white so the row can tint them the way `assets/social` already does.
- `NOTICE`, `ATTRIBUTION.md` and `assets/icons/README.md` record where each icon came from, and
  `assets/icons/LICENSE-Lucide.txt` carries Lucide's ISC notice and its Feather lineage.
- Nothing is drawn as a character, so no font has to carry a symbol.

No behaviour changes: same rows, same order, same actions.

author: Mulyawan-ts
body:
# Add crate-ci/typos spell check to CI

## What

Adds a `typos` job to `ci.yml` and a `typos.toml` config, so a misspelling in a comment, a doc comment, a message or a UI string is caught on the PR instead of living in the tree until someone notices it.

```
crate-ci/typos@685eb3d55be2f85191e8c84acb9f44d7756f84ab # v1.29.4
```

SHA-pinned like the other third-party actions in this repo (`actions/checkout`, `Swatinem/rust-cache`). Runs on `ubuntu-latest`, no Rust toolchain needed, finishes in seconds.

## Why

I ran `typos` over the whole tree first, and it found no English typo, so there is nothing to fix in this PR. That is the point of adding the check: cheap insurance, and the interesting part was the config, not the findings.

## The config, and why it needs one

Two kinds of exemption, both deliberate.

**The translation catalogs are excluded.** `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv` has nine languages in its second column (German, French, Polish, Portuguese, Spanish, Czech, Hungarian, Japanese, Chinese), and `typos` reads every file type. Without the exclusion it reports about 90 correct words as English misspellings. `docs/brand/LICENSE-brand.txt` is excluded too: it is a verbatim trademark licence, not text we are free to edit.

**The prose is British, the code is American.** This repo writes "colour", "centred", "licence", "honoured", "neighbour" in comments and doc comments, but keeps `Color32`, `center()`, "notarized" and "localization" in code and in Apple notary terms. `typos` has one locale per project, so `locale = "en-us"` plus an explicit list of the British spellings in `[default.extend-words]` is the only combination that reads the tree as intended. The i18n tests under `crates/ui-egui/tests/` assert on the same translations, so they need `[default.extend-identifiers]` for the German, French, Spanish and Polish words that appear in UI labels.

title: fix(linux): honour desktop X11 scale factor and propagate to launched…
author: ccsimenson
body:
## Summary

On Linux, `winit`'s X11 backend ignores desktop DPI settings (`Xft.dpi`, `GDK_SCALE`, `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`) when `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` is unset and instead computes the scale factor from the monitor's EDID physical millimeter dimensions reported by XRandR.

Many HDMI monitors and TVs (such as Samsung 16:9 displays) encode their aspect ratio (`160 mm × 90 mm`, i.e., `16 cm × 9 cm`) in the EDID physical size fields rather than actual physical millimeters. On a `1920×1080` screen reporting `160 mm × 90 mm`, `winit` computes `304.8 DPI` (`scale_factor = 3.1667`), causing ArtCraft Launcher and every Craft Suite app (which force X11 via `with_x11()` for file drag-and-drop) to open at 2x–3x the size of the screen and persist inflated `inner_size_points` to `app.ron` / `ui.json`.

## Changes

1. **`apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs`**:
   - Add `resolve_x11_scale_factor` and `ensure_x11_scale_factor` to resolve `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` on X11 sessions from `Xft.dpi` (`xrdb -query`), `GDK_SCALE`, or `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`, defaulting to `"1"`.
   - Add unit test `x11_scale_factor_prefers_xft_dpi_then_desktop_env_then_one`.
2. **`crates/native/src/process.rs`**:
   - In `command()`, ensure `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` is propagated when `DISPLAY` is set so Craft Suite apps launched from inside ArtCraft Launcher also avoid XRandR EDID DPI inflation even when the launcher itself runs under Wayland.

title: Settings: one folder for the launcher's files, portable installs included
author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #775 (reported against SoundCraft, but this part is the launcher's).

That report notes two folders for one app, which is exactly what the code does:

```
~/.local/share/artcraft-launcher/                   logs, installed.json, apps/
~/.local/share/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher/    app.ron
```

`Paths::new` joins `DIR` (`"artcraft-launcher"` off macOS and Windows); eframe picks its own folder from the app id, `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher`. Two independent derivations, so the launcher's state ends up split.

### The part that is more than tidiness

**A portable install is not portable in its settings.** `portable_root()` sends data and cache under `ArtCraftLauncherData` beside the executable when `portable.txt` is there, but eframe's folder stays in the user's profile. So a launcher carried on a stick writes its window size, egui memory and settings into every machine it runs on, and finds none of it on the next one.

### What changed

`Paths::settings()` is `<data>/app.ron`, and `NativeOptions::persistence_path` points eframe at it, so the state file sits beside the logs and the manifest and follows the portable root with everything else.

One thing worth flagging for review: eframe's doc comment calls that option

> The folder where `eframe` will store the app state.

but the value goes to `FileStorage::from_ron_filepath`, so it is the **file**. Passing the folder would have written the state as a file named after the folder. There is a note where it is set.

Settings an earlier version left in eframe's folder are adopted once:

- nothing where the launcher now keeps them → the old file is copied over;
- something already there → left alone, so a downgrade and a re-upgrade cannot replace newer settings with older ones;
- nothing to adopt, or the same path twice → a no-op, not an error.

The old file is left where it is: it is small, and an older launcher started again still finds its settings.

author: echelon
body:
Fixes the 4 test failures in the nightly FreeBSD 15 aarch64 run (39360025796).

## 1. No asset picked on FreeBSD aarch64

**Cause:** `Platform::tokens()` in `crates/core/src/platform.rs` mapped `(FreeBsd, X64)` to `freebsd-x86_64` and every other FreeBSD architecture to nothing. Since 2026-10-18 every Craft App release ships `<app>-<ver>-freebsd-aarch64.tar.gz`, but the launcher never picked it. So on FreeBSD aarch64 `planned_download` returned `None`, and the `keep_file` helper in the backend tests panicked. - `(FreeBsd, Arm64)` now maps to `freebsd-aarch64`, picked the same way x86_64 is.
- There is no fallback between architectures in either direction.
- The download-source rules are unchanged.

- The synthetic release in the backend tests now includes the `freebsd-aarch64` token.

- Self-update doesn't pick assets on FreeBSD. It shows the download link instead.

title: fix(windows): retry busy download renames and log Windows Installer runs
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #686

## Problem
On Windows, no Craft app installs. The error is either `couldn't save the download (Access denied. (os error 5))` or `the Windows Installer stopped with error 1603`. Running the launcher as admin doesn't help.

## Changes
- **`http.rs`**: after the checksum passes, the rename from `.part` to the final file now goes through `rename_retrying`. On Windows only, it retries errors 5 (access denied) and 32 (sharing violation) with backoff (100 ms doubling, about 6 s in total). Antivirus scanners commonly hold a freshly written installer open, which makes the rename fail with exactly this error. This is inferred, not reproduced.
- **`install.rs`**: `msiexec` now runs with `/l*v <package>.log`, and errors other than cancel now end with the log's path. 1603 is the installer's generic failure code, so the log is the only way to find the real cause. The existing 7-day download cleanup removes old logs.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native`: 155 pass. The MSI command argument test is updated for the log flag.
- The Windows-only code is not built locally (C dependencies need `lib.exe`), so the Windows CI job is what compiles it.
- Not yet tested on a real Windows machine. Needs a retest from the reporter, plus the MSI log if 1603 persists.

Both release tools were downloaded at whatever version was current, with no check. They are now pinned the same way as in designcraft:

title: Linux and FreeBSD install: run pkexec and package tools from the system directories
author: aiongg
body:
`pkexec` looks a bare program name up on the caller's `PATH`, and the launcher found `pkexec` itself on `PATH` too. Both now come only from a fixed list of root-owned directories:

- Linux: `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/sbin`.
- FreeBSD: the same four, then `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/local/sbin`, because FreeBSD's packages (polkit's `pkexec` at `/usr/local/bin/pkexec` among them) install there.

What uses the list:

- `run_as_root` hands `pkexec` an absolute path. A bare name is looked up in those directories; a relative path with folders in it is refused. The FreeBSD tree install and removal already pass `/bin/cp` and `/bin/rm` by absolute path.
- The checks that decide which package formats can be installed (`apt-get`, `dpkg`, `rpm`, `dnf`, `zypper`, `pacman`) look in the same directories, so the launcher offers only what it can run.
- `pkexec` is found in the same directories, both where it runs a command and where the launcher decides whether a system-wide install is possible (Linux packages; on FreeBSD, the `/usr/local` tree install, which falls back to `~/.local` without `pkexec`).

Unchanged: `pacman -Si` (run as the user) and the paru/yay hint still use `PATH`.

NixOS: its `pkexec` is the wrapper in `/run/wrappers/bin`, which the list doesn't include, so the launcher treats NixOS as having no polkit. That changes no install choice: NixOS's `os-release` names no `.deb`/`.rpm`/Arch family, so it was offered Flatpak and AppImage before and still is. The same holds for any distro whose `apt-get`, `rpm` or `pacman` live outside the four Linux directories: it loses its native-package install and keeps Flatpak and AppImage.

## Checks

- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo check -p artcraft-launcher-native --target x86_64-unknown-freebsd` (with `--tests` too): builds; the two `self_update.rs` dead-code warnings it prints come from unchanged code. Not run on FreeBSD itself.

author: MMexicann

`FeedThrottle` accepts a 24-hour `Retry-After`, but restarting discarded that valid saved cooldown because `load()` only allowed deadlines twelve hours ahead. A restart one minute after the response could immediately request the feed instead of waiting another 86,340 seconds.

Accept saved deadlines through the supported `Retry-After` maximum plus the existing 50% jitter, using saturating addition at the clock limit. Add regressions for restarts at jitter values 0, 0.5 and 0.99, and for a saved deadline near the clock limit.

Validation:

- Before the fix: all 12 existing throttle tests passed; the new regression failed (0 versus 86,340 seconds remaining).
- The clock-boundary regression reproduces an arithmetic-overflow panic before saturating the guard.
- Native tests: 139 passed, 3 ignored, 1 filtered. The unfiltered initial run fails only the existing Windows junction test because this sandbox denies `mklink`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and native all-targets Clippy with `-D warnings` pass.
- `cargo xtask wasm` passes for both core and web.

title: fix(ui): drop a saved Installed/Updates/Not installed filter on the desktop too
author: akdavid4real
body:
## What happens

After updating to 0.6.0 on Linux (AppImage), the grid shows only the installed apps, with no "Not installed" section and no way to bring the others back. The settings file still holds `filter:Installed`, saved by an older version that had the filter dropdown.

## Why

`LauncherUi::new` already resets a saved filter the toolbar no longer offers (#527, `e00be80`). Tests that set `settings.filter` directly to bring cards on screen still work, because the reset only applies to loaded settings, not at draw time.

title: fix(linux): links bring the browser in front of the launcher
author: benandez
body:
Closes #698

## Problem
On Linux (esp. KDE Plasma/Wayland) clicking any link in the launcher opened the browser *behind* the window; KWin only flashed it in the taskbar. eframe opens links without an activation token and drops winit's `ActivationTokenDone` event.

## Fix — port of MailCraft #144 (UCS-Care-Group/mailcraft#167)
- `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/browser.rs` (new, Linux/FreeBSD only): takes egui's `OpenUrl` commands out of each frame, asks winit for an activation token per link, then starts `xdg-open` (or `flatpak-spawn --host xdg-open` in Flatpak) with it in `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` + `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID`. Fallback to the old path (`webbrowser`, as eframe did) when: no token within 1 s, `$BROWSER` set, non-http(s) address, or `xdg-open` fails. URLs never logged.
- `main.rs`: on Linux/FreeBSD the window runs on our own winit event loop via `eframe::create_native` + `run_app_on_demand` (thread-local loop reused across the launcher's window passes, as eframe does), wrapped in `WithTokens` to catch the token. Windows/macOS still use `eframe::run_native`.
- `Cargo.toml`: `[patch.crates-io] winit` → `UCS-Care-Group/winit` @ `bb472d9` (0.30.13 + latest-click serial on the token request, which KWin requires). Same patch MailCraft ships; drop when upstream winit does it.
- `flake.nix`: `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit = true` for that git dep.
- Discord deep link and tray menu links unchanged. Tray links are out of scope: `ksni`/`tray-icon` can't receive the panel's activation token (https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/698#issuecomment-6303073053).

title: Settings: list the languages alphabetically by their own name
author: nikolainyegaard
body:
The Language picker in Settings listed the languages in registry order, which is the order they were added: Русский and 简体中文 first, Deutsch fourth.

## Change

`Lang::for_picker` returns the languages in picker order: English first, as the source language and the fallback, then the rest sorted by their own name with Latin accents folded, so Čeština is under C and Magyar under M. Names in other scripts follow the Latin ones in code point order, which puts Русский and then the CJK languages at the end without a special rule. The order follows the native name even where the picker shows a CJK language's English name because no font for it is installed, so the list does not reorder when a font appears. The registry keeps its order.

## Test

`picker_lists_english_first_then_names_alphabetically` checks the properties rather than a fixed list, so adding a language cannot make it stale: English first, the keys sorted, Čeština before Deutsch, Magyar after Français, Português before Русский, Русский before 日本語.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui --lib -- i18n::`: 31 passed

title: Use jiff instead of hand-rolled UTC conversion
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Follow-up to storytold/cadcraft#1785 (see reference PR storytold/cadcraft#1789).

## Summary
`crates/core/src/time.rs` and `xtask/src/local.rs` carried their own copies of
Howard Hinnant's civil / days-from-civil algorithm (the `719_468` / `146_097`
magic numbers) to turn GitHub timestamps into dates and back. This routes that
through a real date crate.

Because the launcher already depends on **jiff** (0.2, in `ui-egui` for the
system time zone), I used jiff here rather than adding `chrono`, so the tree
keeps a single time crate. jiff is lifted to a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry
and `ui-egui` now takes it with `{ workspace = true }`; `core` and `xtask` get it
the same way.

Replaced functions and their formats:
- `crates/core/src/time.rs`:
  - `parse_rfc3339` — its `days_from_civil` helper now builds a `jiff::civil::Date`
    and measures the days to the epoch. The day-past-month-length rollover the old
    arithmetic allowed (`2026-02-30` → `2026-03-02`) is preserved by adding
    `(day-1)` days to the first of the month, and the rest of the RFC 3339 field
    parsing and validation (including a leap second) is untouched.
  - `civil_from_unix(i64) -> (i64, u32, u32)` — now pure civil-date arithmetic on
    `jiff::civil::Date` (no time zone), feeding `format_date` ("Oct 8, 2026").
- `xtask/src/local.rs`:
  - `rfc3339(i64)` — the local mirror feed's `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` timestamps,
    now via `jiff::civil::Date`.

`core` uses only civil-date math (no time zone), so the wasm build is unaffected;
`web-time` is untouched. `AGENTS.md` gains the rule that time goes through jiff
and nobody hand-rolls calendar math (its `CLAUDE.md` is a pointer to AGENTS.md, so
it was left as-is).

title: An argument that is not UTF-8 is ignored, not the end of the start-up
author: Hamza0101
body:
`std::env::args` panics on an argument that is not valid UTF-8, and it panics while **collecting** the arguments — before the launcher looks at what it was given. So any start-up with such an argument ended here:

```
$ artcraft-launcher /tmp/café.png --version        # that é as a single Latin-1 byte
[ERROR artcraft_launcher::logging] internal error: panicked at library/std/src/env.rs:878:51:
    called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "/tmp/caf\xE9.png"
exit 101
```

Measured on `main`, with the argument before or after `--version` or alone — the window never opens, and the launcher's own panic hook files it as an internal error.

A desktop start-up brings along what it brings along: `-psn_0_…` from Finder when a bundle is opened, a file dropped on the icon, an old login entry's leftovers. The launcher already ignores all of it — it looks for `--version`/`-V` and `--hidden` and nothing else — so an argument it cannot read is one it would have ignored anyway. It now comes through `args_os`, and what cannot be read is logged and dropped:

```
[WARN artcraft_launcher] ignoring an argument that is not valid UTF-8: /tmp/caf�.png
artcraft-launcher 0.6.1
```

### Why it matters beyond the tail case

`packaging/linux/package.sh` runs `"$STAGE/usr/bin/$PKG" --version` as the smoke test for every staged build, including under an emulator for a foreign architecture. That check passes or fails on whether the binary can read its own arguments.

### Tests

`apps/artcraft-launcher/tests/arguments.rs`, the app's first integration test — `--version` is the one thing the launcher does without opening a window, so it is what a test can ask for from here:

title: fix(windows): self-update runs no PowerShell and installs only files signed like the launcher
author: dotCooCoo
body:
On Windows the launcher finished its own update with a detached `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -Command …` (`crates/native/src/self_update.rs`, `windows_helper`). The script waited for the launcher to exit, ran the new MSI or `Expand-Archive`d the portable zip over the launcher's folder, deleted the download and started the new exe. A hidden PowerShell with an execution-policy bypass, followed by running and deleting a downloaded file, is a sequence antivirus heuristics score, and the command line sits in the signed `artcraft-launcher.exe` as a string. Related: #251.

## Fix

- The update helper is a copy of the launcher, put in `<cache>\launcher-update-helper` and started with `--finish-update`. `main()` hands that flag to the helper before logging, the single-instance claim and the window.
- The helper waits for the old process with `OpenProcess` and `WaitForSingleObject` (`winsafe`; the workspace forbids `unsafe`), then runs `msiexec /i … /passive /norestart` and checks its exit code, or unpacks the portable zip with the checks `portable::extract` already applies to app installs. Then it starts the launcher again.
- The helper finishes only the launcher's own update. The exe must be this launcher's MSI or portable installation, and the helper, the download and the staging folder must be in that installation's cache. The MSI, every program in the portable zip, and the exe it starts must carry a valid Authenticode signature from the helper's own publisher (`verifysign`, through WinTrust). Without these checks, any program could use the signed launcher to run an arbitrary MSI or exe.
- Before it quits, the launcher checks its own signature, the installed exe and the new MSI. A build without a signature now reports "this copy of ArtCraft Launcher isn't signed …, so it doesn't install updates" instead of updating. Release builds are signed.
- Before it quits, the launcher also checks that the helper, which finds …

title: fix(windows): read a portable app's version without starting PowerShell
author: dotCooCoo
body:
After unpacking a portable app, the launcher compares the exe's ProductVersion with the release (`install.rs`, the portable arm of `install`). `detect::windows::executable_version` read it by starting a hidden `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` that called `FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo`. That costs a PowerShell start on every portable install, and a hidden PowerShell started by a downloaded exe is a pattern antivirus heuristics score. Related: #251.

## Fix

`executable_version` reads the ProductVersion string from the file's VERSIONINFO with `GetFileVersionInfo` and `VerQueryValue` (`winsafe`, since the workspace forbids `unsafe`): in the languages the file lists, then in the string tables .NET's `FileVersionInfo` also tries (040904B0, 040904E4, 04090000). No process is started.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

title: security: confine release/feed download URLs and bind installed artifact version
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Hardens the update/install path against two related repository-confinement weaknesses in feed and GitHub release handling, plus a version-binding gap.

Three findings, one subsystem (release/feed URL trust), so they are fixed together:

1. **Release JSON URL traversal (CWE-180)** — `release_from_value` accepted `browser_download_url` on a raw `starts_with(prefix)` check.
2. **Feed URL traversal (CWE-180)** — `FeedRelease::to_release` used the same raw-prefix check; a feed could advertise a legitimate tag yet point an asset at `.../releases/download/../../../ATTACKER/REPO/...`, which the Linux AppImage self-update then downloads and executes.
3. **Artifact version not bound to the release** — the installer persisted `release.version` without confirming the downloaded artifact actually was that version, letting a controller advertise a new version while shipping an older official build (bypassing the downgrade guard).

## Changes

- Add `release::download_url_under` and `download_url_under_mirror`. A download is accepted only when the text after the approved prefix is exactly `<tag>/<name>`: two non-empty path segments, no `.`/`..` traversal, no extra slashes, no query/fragment/backslash, and no percent-encoded separators (`%2f`/`%5c`). `release_from_value` and `FeedRelease::to_release` now share this.
- Add `bind_artifact_version` in the native installer: before downloading, reject an artifact whose filename-encoded version or URL release tag disagrees with `release.version`.

## Tests

- `release::tests::traversal_cannot_escape_the_repository`
- `feed::tests::a_feed_url_cannot_traverse_out_of_the_repository`
- `install::tests::install_rejects_an_artifact_whose_version_is_not_the_advertised_one`
- Full `artcraft-launcher-core` (41) and `artcraft-launcher-native` (161) lib test suites pass; `cargo clippy` clean on both crates.

title: security: bound decoded feed size, screenshot dimensions, and locale tag matching
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Three resource-exhaustion (DoS) findings that share the untrusted-input handling in update/feed and details-page rendering.

1. **Decoded feed/API size not bounded (CWE-409)** — `read_to_string().limit(MAX_SMALL)` silently truncates at 4 MiB, and with ureq's transparent gzip a small compressed response can decode far beyond the compressed byte count.
2. **Screenshot decode bomb (CWE-789)** — screenshot bytes were accepted on the JPEG signature plus a 2 MiB byte cap, but a tiny JPEG can declare 65,535 × 65,535; `egui_extras`/`image` allocate `width × height × channels` from the header *before* decoding, turning a 2 MiB response into a multi-gigabyte allocation.
3. **Quadratic locale matching (CWE-400)** — `candidates()` built every progressively shorter prefix of an unbounded URL `lang` value, allocating O(n²).

## Changes

- `http.rs`: add `read_text_capped`, which reads one byte past the cap and rejects an oversized **decoded** body before parsing. Used by `get_api`, `get_feed`, `get_text`.

title: security: harden local install and packaging against filesystem attacks
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Three local filesystem-safety findings across install and packaging.

1. **Tar installer symlink binary (CWE-59)** — `unpack_tree` set the app binary executable with `std::fs::set_permissions`, which follows symlinks. An archive whose `bin/<app>` (or an ancestor inside the tree) is a symlink pointing outside the install tree would have its external target changed to mode 0755.
2. **Autostart desktop-entry injection (CWE-74)** — the Linux login entry built `Exec="{exe}"` escaping only `"`, so an executable path containing a line break could introduce a second `Exec=` key that the desktop runs at login.
3. **Signing certificate temp file (CWE-377)** — `import-cert.sh` wrote the decoded `.p12` to a fixed, predictable name in a shared temp root, where another local user could pre-create the destination and capture the secret bytes.

## Changes

- `install.rs`: `make_runnable_within` rejects any symlinked component between the tree root and the binary, and only chmods a verified regular file at that path. The external target of a symlinked binary is never touched.
- `login.rs`: use `desktop_entry::exec_quote` (spec-compliant, refuses control characters) for the autostart `Exec=` line, erroring out when the path can't be represented safely.
- `packaging/macos/import-cert.sh`: create a private `mktemp -d` directory under the temp root and write the certificate and keychain inside it; remove the certificate once imported.

## Tests

- `install::tests::a_tarball_binary_that_is_a_symlink_out_of_the_tree_is_refused` (asserts the external file keeps its original 0600 mode)
- Existing `desktop_entry::quotes_exec_paths_per_the_spec` already covers newline rejection now used by the autostart writer.
- `shellcheck` clean on `import-cert.sh`; native lib suite (161) passes; `cargo clippy` clean.

title: security: authenticate single-instance replace and bound the local mirror server
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Two local-service hardening findings in IPC and developer tooling.

1. **Single-instance replacement authority (CWE-862)** — the listener on the fixed loopback port `127.0.0.1:47413` granted a `Replace` request (which can make an idle launcher quit) based on the peer's claimed version alone, with no peer authentication. A different local OS account could send `hello <newer-version>` and make the victim's idle launcher exit.
2. **Local mirror server resource exhaustion (CWE-770)** — `xtask local serve` spawned a thread per connection with no admission limit, request reads had no deadline (idle clients held handler threads indefinitely), and a failed thread spawn could panic the listener.

## Changes

- `single_instance.rs`: a per-user token now gates `Replace`. It lives in the user's own data folder, created owner-only (0600 on Unix); the second start echoes it in its `hello`, and the primary only honours `Replace` when the token matches. An unauthenticated local peer may still bring the window forward (`Show`, harmless) but can never quit the launcher. The token is derived without adding an RNG crate, hashing OS-seeded `RandomState` through `sha2`. `claim`'s public signature is unchanged.
- `xtask/src/local.rs`: bounded handler cap (64; excess connections get `503 Service Unavailable`), a 15s request-header read deadline that is lifted before streaming the response body so legitimate downloads aren't cut, and graceful handling of thread-spawn failure instead of panicking the listener.

## Tests

- `single_instance::tests::a_replace_requires_the_same_users_token` (unauthenticated/absent token → `Show`, not `Replace`)
- `single_instance::tests::a_fresh_secret_is_a_distinct_nonempty_hex_string`
- Updated existing single-instance tests to carry a token; all 10 pass.
- native lib suite (162) passes; xtask checks clean; `cargo clippy` clean on both crates.

title: security: reject shell metacharacters in opened web links (WSL cmd.exe injection)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Feed notice links and release-note hyperlinks are forwarded to the system opener when the user clicks them. The pinned `webbrowser` crate's WSL fallback passes the URL to `cmd.exe /c start` while escaping only `^` and `&`, so a `|` (or other metacharacter) in an otherwise valid `https://` URL becomes a command separator and executes a Windows command when clicked (CWE-78).

## Approach

Rather than depend on the third-party opener to neutralise the URL, refuse any link containing a shell/cmd metacharacter at the validation boundary, where a legitimate `https` web link never needs one:

- `release::safe_web_link` (release notes) now rejects shell metacharacters (`| & ; < > ( ) $ backtick " ' ^ ! * { } [ ]`) via the shared `release::is_shell_meta`, on top of the existing scheme/host/whitespace checks.
- The feed notice link filter (`RawNotice::into_notice`) routes through the same rule and also rejects control characters.

Both paths that can carry a remote link to `OpenUrl` (feed announcements/alerts and release-note hyperlinks) are now sanitised at ingestion, so no accepted link can carry shell syntax to the opener.

## Tests

- `release::tests::only_plain_https_links_pass` extended with `|`, `&`, backtick, `$()`, `;`, `>` cases.
- `feed::tests::reads_notices_and_renames` extended with a `https://…/a|calc.exe` alert link that must be dropped.
- `artcraft-launcher-core` (39) and `artcraft-launcher-ui-egui` (47) lib suites pass; `cargo clippy` clean.

title: FreeBSD: package the aarch64 cross build (craft-common-actions#39)
author: zuujiscom
body:
Part of https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions/issues/39

## What happens today
FreeBSD aarch64 was dropped from releases because the emulated aarch64 VM took over 5 hours. storytold/craft-common-actions#50 now cross-compiles aarch64 inside the KVM-accelerated x86_64 FreeBSD VM, opt-in through the `freebsd-architectures` input of `release.yml`. Its cross toolchain step exports `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=aarch64-unknown-freebsd` before `packaging/freebsd/package.sh` runs. With aarch64 turned on, this app's script would:
- name the archive after `uname -m`, which is always amd64 in the guest, so the release job fails its archive-name check;
- read the binaries from `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release`, but cargo writes a cross build to `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/aarch64-unknown-freebsd/release`.

## Change
`packaging/freebsd/package.sh` only:
- the arch comes from `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` when it is set (`aarch64-unknown-freebsd` → `aarch64`, `x86_64-unknown-freebsd` → `x86_64`), else from `uname -m` as before;
- a target other than `aarch64-unknown-freebsd` or `x86_64-unknown-freebsd` (a Linux or macOS triple, a bare arch, another FreeBSD triple) is refused with exit 2, and the target is read before `uname -m`, so an unsupported host does not block a valid cross build;
- binaries are read from `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/${CARGO_BUILD_TARGET:+$CARGO_BUILD_TARGET/}release`.

Without `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` the script behaves exactly as before, so x86_64 releases are unchanged. This PR does not opt the app into aarch64: that is a one-line `freebsd-architectures: '["x86_64","aarch64"]'` in the release caller, to do once this is merged.

`strip` is safe on the aarch64 binaries: FreeBSD 15.1's `/usr/bin/strip` is llvm-strip, which strips other-architecture ELFs. Tested in a FreeBSD 15.1 VM: it stripped a foreign-arch executable with exit 0 (the call keeps its `|| true` anyway).

## Testing

- `--dry-run`: output identical to `main` for…

title: native: refuse plain-HTTP redirects on every HTTPS agent
author: hakarrr
body:
None of the ureq agents built in `crates/native/src/http.rs` set `https_only`, and ureq 3's default is `false`, so an HTTPS request redirected to `http://` was followed in plain text. That covers `get_text` (which fetches `SHA256SUMS.txt`) and `download`: the checksum and payload guarantees depended on every server in the redirect chain behaving.

Each agent now sets `https_only`. Plain HTTP stays available where it is legitimate: a developer's loopback mirror (feature `local-mirror`) and this module's test server (`cfg(test)`).

A new test pins the refused-before-connect behavior the agents rely on; it builds its own agent because the crate's agents allow loopback HTTP under `cfg(test)`.

Tests: `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native` - 165 passed, 0 failed, including the new `https_only_refuses_plain_http_before_connecting`.

title: macOS: the Dock icon brings the window back after closing it (#456)
author: EricKaden
body:
Fixes #456. Also reported as #478, #622, #744 and #763.

## The problem

On macOS, closing the window with the red button keeps the launcher running in the menu bar, but clicking its Dock icon afterward (or opening it again from Finder or Spotlight) brings nothing back. The only ways back are the menu-bar icon → "Show ArtCraft Launcher", or quitting and relaunching.

The window is ordered out (`ViewportCommand::Visible(false)`). When the Dock icon is clicked, AppKit sends the app a "reopen" Apple Event (`applicationShouldHandleReopen:hasVisibleWindows:`), and neither winit 0.30 nor eframe passes it on. Handling it directly would take registering an Apple Event handler or adding a method to winit's app delegate, and both need `unsafe`, which the workspace forbids.

## The fix

On macOS, closing to the tray now hides the app, as ⌘H does, instead of ordering the window out. macOS brings a hidden app back by itself, window and all, when its Dock icon is clicked, when it's opened again from Finder or Spotlight, or when it's picked with ⌘Tab. "Show ArtCraft Launcher" unhides the app before showing the window. Everything goes through safe `objc2-app-kit` calls (`NSApplication::hide`/`unhide`) in a new `hiding.rs`, next to `spaces.rs`. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

A visible difference: after the red button, the app you were using before the launcher becomes active again, as after ⌘H, instead of the launcher staying active with no window.

## Not changed: starting hidden at login

A start in the tray (`--hidden`) still orders the window out, as before. Hiding the app there doesn't work reliably: the app is still being activated while it starts, and that unhides it a few frames later, window and all, so the window would appear at login. After the window has been shown once, closing it goes through the new path.

## About #667

I built #667 on top of current `main` and tested it on macOS 27 (Apple Silicon). After the red button, clicking the Dock icon left 0 windows on sc…

title: Windows: keep pinned taskbar icons across updates
author: gossotjeanbaptiste
body:
Fixes #643.

## Cause

The MSI's Start Menu and desktop shortcuts took their icon from the WiX `<Icon Id="ArtCraftLauncherIcon.exe">`. Windows Installer caches that file in `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Installer\{ProductCode}\`. Every update is a major upgrade with a new ProductCode, and the old folder is deleted. The Start Menu shortcut is reinstalled and points at the new folder. A taskbar pin, though, is a copy of the shortcut that no update refreshes, so it kept pointing at a deleted icon. Explorer's icon cache hides this until it is flushed, which is why the bug looks intermittent. Details and paths from a real install are in the issue.

## Change

- `packaging/windows/artcraft-launcher.wxs`: the two shortcuts no longer set `Icon`/`IconIndex`, so they use the icon embedded in `artcraft-launcher.exe` (`build.rs`; `package.ps1` sets `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_REQUIRE_WINRES=1`). The exe's path stays the same across updates. The `<Icon>` stays for `ARPPRODUCTICON` (Apps & features), which isn't affected.
- `packaging/windows/check-icons.ps1`: fails on a shortcut that names an MSI `<Icon>`, and runs the ICE50 extension check on `ARPPRODUCTICON` instead.

## Testing

- `check-icons.ps1` passes.
- Not yet tested with a built MSI: install, pin, then upgrade to a second build. The pin should keep its icon.

Pins that are already broken stay broken, because an update never touches them. Affected users need to unpin and pin again once after installing this version.

title: xtask local: order pre-releases by semver (rc.10 after rc.9)
author: smittie2000
body:
`cargo xtask local` compared pre-release tags as plain strings, so `1.0.0-rc.10` sorted before `1.0.0-rc.9`. `compare_versions` decides which mirrored build `status` shows as the newest and which builds `prune` keeps, so a tenth release candidate would have been treated as older than the ninth and pruned first.

title: portable: a network-share install matches its canonical path
author: smittie2000
body:
`same_windows_path` in `portable.rs` stripped only a leading `\\?\`. For a folder on a network share, `canonicalize` returns `\\?\UNC\server\share\...`, which became `UNC\server\share\...` and never matched the recorded `\\server\share\...`. So updating or removing a portable app installed on a share failed with "The recorded portable folder resolves through a changed alias".

It now maps `\\?\UNC\` back to `\\` before comparing, matching the prefix in any case as Windows does (`\\?\unc\` too); `\\?\C:\...` is handled as before. A new Windows test covers a drive path, a share path (upper- and lower-case prefix) and a different drive. The share cases fail on the old code.

`dunce::simplified` doesn't help here: it only simplifies drive paths and leaves `\\?\UNC\...` unchanged (checked against dunce 1.0).

Found with apidex's docs search (Windows path comparison).

Checked with:
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native`
- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check -p artcraft-launcher-native`

title: Timestamps saved to disk never wrap the schedule arithmetic (#774)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #774

## What was wrong

Two places subtracted a timestamp loaded from disk without sanitising it (per the audit in
#774):

1. **Feed throttle** (`crates/native/src/feed_throttle.rs`): `load` only dropped a saved
   `not_before` *far in the future*; a value at or below zero survived, and `wait`'s
   `at - now` then wrapped — `not_before` near `i64::MIN` panicked a debug build and, wrapped
   in a release build, returned a centuries-long wait so the release feed was never asked
   again.
2. **Update-check schedule** (`crates/ui-egui/src/app.rs`): `now - t >= every` — a saved
   `last_check` in the future (an edited `app.ron`, a clock that ran fast and was later
   corrected) postponed every periodic check until real time caught up, and `i64::MIN`
   panicked the subtraction. The issue also named the two rescan comparisons sharing the
   pattern.

## What changed

- `feed_throttle.rs`: `load` now drops any saved wait outside
  `0..=now.saturating_add(2 * MAX_THROTTLE_BACKOFF)` (negative or far-future), and `wait`
  computes `at.saturating_sub(now).max(0)`. Legitimate saved waits are unaffected (they are
  always `now + backoff ≤ now + 6 h`).
- `app.rs`: the condition is now a small pure predicate, `update_check_due(last, now,
  every)`: a time in the future is due, `i64::MIN` saturates (due), everything else waits
  out the interval as before. The two `last_detect` comparisons use `saturating_sub`.

## Tests added

- `crates/native/src/feed_throttle.rs`:
  `an_absurdly_old_saved_not_before_is_no_wait` — a saved `not_before` of `i64::MIN` (or
  `-60`) means no wait. Panicked before the fix at the exact `wait` line named in the
  issue (`at - now`).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/app.rs` (new `tests` module):
  `a_check_is_due_after_its_interval` (behaviour unchanged for sane times) and
  `a_saved_time_in_the_future_or_at_i64_min_never_postpones_a_check` — future and
  `i64::MIN`/`i64::MAX` times are due; the `i64::MIN` case panicked before the fix.

title: Windows: one UAC prompt per batch of MSIs, then install silently (#67)
author: epell-development
body:
Update all used to ask for administrator permission once per app, with a Windows Installer window for each. MSI jobs that are ready together now become one batch: the launcher starts itself elevated once (`--install-msis`, via PowerShell's runas), and that helper installs each MSI with `msiexec /qn /norestart`, writing each exit code to a results file so one failed app doesn't fail the others. The cards say "Waiting for permission…" while the prompt is up; declining it cancels the batch.

- queue: jobs take a Ticket before their download; a batch waits while any ticket for its command is out, so Update all is one batch however long each download takes. Batches can report per-job outcomes and stages.
- msi_batch: the elevated helper trusts only its arguments: canonical absolute .msi paths and lowercase SHA-256s, each MSI opened (no write, rename or delete sharing) and re-hashed through that handle, held while msiexec runs; results and logs are created new; msiexec and PowerShell are found through HKLM's SystemRoot.
- Running apps are left out just before the prompt. If the prompt can't be shown (PowerShell blocked by policy), each MSI installs as before.
- Linux: the same tickets mean packages started together share one pkexec prompt (reported on Fedora in #67).

Fixes #67 (and its duplicates #104, #124, #254, #433, #538, #550).

**Update all** on Windows used to ask for administrator permission once per app, each with its own Windows Installer window. title: Backend: Clear busy state when a worker panics (#780)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #780

## What was wrong
The native backend cleared `checking`, `detecting` and each `jobs` entry as the last statements of its worker closures. A panic in a worker skipped them, so update checks stopped until restart, an app showed as busy forever, and a stuck `jobs` entry held up `claim_restart` for self-update.

## What changed
As the issue suggests, each flag and each `jobs` entry is now owned by a small drop guard (`BusyGuard`, `JobGuard` in `crates/native/src/backend.rs`), like `Turn` and `PicturesBusy` in `queue.rs`. The guard is created before the thread is spawned and moved into it, so the state is cleared on unwind too. On the normal path the guard is dropped explicitly where the old `store(false)` / `remove(...)` lines were, so the order is unchanged: `checking` is clear before `CheckFinished`, and the job entry is gone before `JobFinished` / `LauncherRestarting`. Covered: detection, update check, install/uninstall jobs and launcher self-update.

## Tests
- `a_panicking_detection_worker_releases_its_busy_flag`, `a_panicking_check_worker_releases_its_busy_flag`, `a_panicking_job_worker_removes_its_busy_entry`: inject a panic through the backend waker on the worker's first event. All 3 failed before the fix.
- `job_finished_is_emitted_after_its_busy_entry_is_removed`: checks the normal-path order.

Run: `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native panicking_`

## Counts
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native`: 173 → 177 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: Tests: retry the version probe of a script a test just wrote (ETXTBSY)
author: echelon
body:
`detect::linux_tests::reads_binary_version_when_the_cli_uses_the_display_name_or_a_former_id` fails now and then (seen locally while testing today's merges). It passes when run alone.

**Cause:** the test writes a shell script and runs it right away. title: Add an Android app shell
author: tzhazuma
body:
This adds `apps/craft-launcher-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window, plus the platform seams the native crate needs to exist on Android at all.

It has been used to ship Android builds of the whole suite (launcher, PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft and the rest) on arm64 Android 14 for a while, so the shape is tested even if the code is new here.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point** — the Rust crate builds as `libmain.so` and is loaded with `System.loadLibrary`; `android_main` is the usual `android-activity` entry.
- **Fonts** — Android does not expose the Unix font directories, so the CJK faces in `/system/fonts` are added as candidates. (`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_font.rs`)
- **Starting an installed app** — on Android the app *is* a package, so `install::launch` cannot exec a path. The Activity is asked to `startActivity`; the two halves talk through a request file because the crate forbids `unsafe` and reaching `PackageManager` needs JNI. (`crates/native/src/android.rs`)
- **Paths** — `dirs` answers nothing on Android and an app cannot write `/tmp`, so the data directory is registered explicitly.
- **APK assets** — `PackageKind::Apk` and asset-name parsing for `.apk` releases.

## What is deliberately not here

Any port-specific configuration. The Android build shipping today hardcodes its own release repository and disables the upstream feed; those are local product decisions and are excluded, so this change is only "the platform exists", not "the platform behaves like my fork".

## Open questions for maintainers

1. Is an Android target something you want in-tree, or would you rather keep it as a separate fork? If the latter, close this and we will keep maintaining it downstream.
2. `install::launch` currently needs the request-file bridge because of the `forbid(unsafe_code)` in the workspace. If you would accept a narrow `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` module for JNI, the bridge could be replaced with a dir…

title: macOS: option to hide the Dock icon while in the menu bar
author: mtbhuskies
body:
## What

A new macOS-only setting under **Settings → Running in the background**: **Hide the Dock icon while in the menu bar** (off by default).

With it on, closing the window to the menu bar takes ArtCraft Launcher out of the Dock and the app switcher, so it runs from its menu bar icon alone. Opening the window from the menu bar brings the Dock icon back while the window is open, so an open window still shows in Cmd-Tab and keeps its menu bar menus.

## How

- `LSUIElement` stays unset, as `AGENTS.md` requires. The new `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/dock.rs` switches the activation policy at runtime instead: accessory in `Shell::put_away`, regular in `Shell::show`. It uses only safe `objc2-app-kit` calls; `Cargo.lock` is unchanged, and the only new thing is the `NSRunningApplication` feature.
- `Settings.hide_dock_icon_in_tray` (default `false`) and a new `Host::has_dock()` (false by default, true on macOS), so the checkbox appears only where it applies. The checkbox is greyed out unless "Keep running in the tray when the window is closed" is on, and the Dock icon is only hidden when there is a tray icon to come back from.
- Both new strings are translated in every `complete_menus` catalog, clean-room from the English. A native speaker's look would be welcome.
- A UI test checks that the setting is hidden where there's no Dock and is off by default.
- `AGENTS.md` now mentions the runtime switch next to the `LSUIElement` rule.
- A separate commit drops an unused `staging_dir` import in `crates/native/src/install.rs` (macOS module). It made `cargo xtask ci` fail clippy on macOS on `main`.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask ci` passes on macOS (fmt, clippy, tests, wasm).
- Tested by hand on macOS: turning the setting on, closing the window and reopening it from the menu bar.

title: security: bound decoded HTTP responses and screenshot decoding (F-006, F-008, F-009)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Resolves CodeRabbit findings **F-006** (CWE-789 JPEG dimension budget evasion via unsupported C3 markers), **F-008** (CWE-409 Decompression bomb in `get_bytes` due to wire-level limit below transparent gzip), and **F-009** (CWE-409 Unbounded decoded bytes during unknown-size chunked downloads).

## Changes
- **`crates/core/src/details.rs`**:
  - In `jpeg_dimensions`, strictly accept only supported SOF markers (SOF0 `0xC0`, SOF1 `0xC1`, SOF2 `0xC2`).
  - Reject unsupported frame markers (such as lossless `0xC3`, `0xC5..=0xCF`) and multiple/conflicting SOF markers to prevent frame smuggling past the screenshot pixel budget.
  - Break gracefully upon reaching `0xDA` (SOS) or entropy-coded scan data.
  - Added unit test cases for `0xC3` and multiple SOF markers.
- **`crates/native/src/http.rs`**:
  - Add `read_bytes_capped` which wraps `body_mut().reader().take(max + 1)` on the decoded stream, preventing transparent gzip decompression from allocating beyond `max`.
  - In `Http::get_bytes`, use `read_bytes_capped` instead of transport-level `.limit()`.
  - In `Http::attempt` (artifact downloads), enforce cumulative decoded bytes ceiling before every disk write, regardless of whether `total` was advertised, preventing unknown-size downloads from exceeding `MAX_DOWNLOAD`.
  - Reject unexpected `Content-Encoding` on binary downloads when `Accept-Encoding: identity` was requested.
  - Added unit tests for oversized byte payload rejection.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-core -p artcraft-launcher-native` passed (all 45 core and 180 native tests).

title: security: bypass proxy for loopback and suppress HTTP wire credential logging (F-003, F-005)

## Summary

title: fix(security): implement mutual challenge-response for single-instance IPC
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves CodeRabbit findings F-016 (CWE-522) and F-017 (CWE-287).

- **F-016 (CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials)**: Previously, the newcomer startup client sent its persistent bearer token in cleartext over the unauthenticated fixed loopback TCP port `47413`. A rogue local listener could capture and replay the credential. Now, the persistent token is never transmitted over TCP.
- **F-017 (CWE-287: Improper Authentication)**: Mutual challenge-response authentication is established between newcomer and running instances. Both parties exchange ephemeral 256-bit nonces and verify SHA-256 HMAC-style proofs using constant-time comparison before granting `Request::Replace`. Stale and replayed authentication responses are rejected.

title: fix(security): enforce bounded reads, deadlines, and terminal escaping in local mirror
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves CodeRabbit findings F-019 (CWE-400), F-020 (CWE-117), and F-021 (CWE-117).

- **F-019 (CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption)**: Replaces `BufReader::read_line` with a bounded byte reader that checks wall-clock deadlines before every read, sets socket read timeouts to the remaining duration, enforces a maximum line length of 8 KiB, and caps total header size at 64 KiB, preventing slowloris connection-slot exhaustion.
- **F-020 & F-021 (CWE-117: Terminal Control / Log Injection)**: Sanitizes `method` and request `path` before emitting to `stderr`, escaping ASCII control characters and ANSI escape sequences to prevent terminal display manipulation and forged status lines.

title: native: serialize single-instance token publication and recover late initialization
author: hakarrr
body:
## Problem

Two starts can both read a missing token, generate different secrets and truncate/write the same file. The listener may retain one secret while later starts read the other, so authenticated version takeover falls back to showing the running launcher. Empty or invalid token contents can reach the same initialization path.

## Change

- Serialize initialization/recovery with a permanent sidecar file lock and reread after acquiring it. Publish a complete token using a temporary file in the same directory, rather than truncating the live token.
- Preserve an existing readable, nonempty token, including when the sidecar cannot be opened. Lock contention waits at most about one second before the existing no-token fallback.
- A primary that started without a token can read a later publication before handling a connection. This retry reads at most 257 bytes, accepts only a regular UTF-8 file up to 256 bytes, never writes/repairs or takes a lock, and never replaces an established in-memory identity.
- Add 12 regression tests covering concurrent initialization/recovery, delayed publication and authenticated takeover, existing-token preservation, invalid/oversized retry reads, contention and owner-only Unix permissions.

## Validation

Exact patch on upstream `f0cb3b0`: unchanged `cargo xtask ci` passed (fmt, strict clippy, workspace tests and WASM check). Native: 197 passed, 3 existing ignored; UI: 50 unit and 63 integration tests passed; core: 46 passed, 1 existing ignored.

https://github.com/hakarrr/craft-launcher/actions/runs/40193948782

The credential-free Linux runner needs `LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` for the existing Unicode process-path test. The untouched baseline fails that test without a locale and passes with UTF-8; the full candidate gate uses UTF-8 without changing or skipping tests. Removing the listener refresh makes the delayed-publication regression fail (`Show` rather than `Replace`). A separate Linux process harness also checked simultaneous…

title: feat(install): let users choose how many downloads run at once
author: dquimper
body:
Follow-up to #403, as suggested in https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/pull/403#issuecomment-6295303424.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR is stacked on #403 and includes its two commits until #403 merges. Only the last commit (`feat(install): let users choose how many downloads run at once`) is new here. I'll rebase it once #403 lands.

## Why

#403 runs one download at a time. On a fast connection, users may want two or more running at once.

## What changes

- **Settings → Updates → "Simultaneous downloads"**, from 1 to 4, default 1. A note under it says downloads running together share the connection. It's shown only in builds that install apps, so not on the web.
- **Raising it** starts waiting downloads right away. **Lowering it** lets running downloads finish, and waiting ones start as slots free up.
- Settings saved before this change load with 1, so behaviour stays the same as #403.

## How

- `protocol`: `BackendOptions.simultaneous_downloads: u8`, next to `prereleases`. 0 counts as 1.
- `downloads.rs`: `Downloads` counts running downloads against a limit, replacing `busy: bool`. A job starts when a slot is free and it ranks first among the waiting jobs. Each start wakes the others in case another slot is free. `set_limit` keeps the value between 1 and `MAX_AT_ONCE` (4).
- `backend.rs`: `Command::Configure` applies the limit to `install::DOWNLOADS`.
- `ui-egui`: the new setting, sent in `configure()`. Both new strings are in all 10 catalogs.

## Testing

- fmt, tests and the wasm check pass. Clippy on macOS still stops at `main`'s unused `staging_dir` import in `install.rs`. With only that lint allowed, it reports nothing.
- 4 new tests in `downloads.rs`: never beyond the limit, a second download running alongside when the limit allows it, raising the limit while a download waits, and the limit kept between 1 and 4.
- 1 new UI test: the setting reaches the backend, and settings without it load as 1.
- Manual test on macOS (arm64):
  - The default is 1. With 2, …

title: fix: respect macOS Low Data Mode for automatic updates

Defer automatic app and ArtCraft Launcher updates on constrained networks, pause active automatic downloads while keeping partial files, and resume when the connection becomes unrestricted. Keep explicit Install, Update, and Resume actions available. Track manual actions per version so a delayed network event cannot restart a download the user paused or cancelled. Original network settings were restored. - Regression tests cover late deferral events after manual cancellation and manual updates paused before any automatic attempt; both failed before the fix and pass afterward. - Linux ARM64: workspace Clippy, 171 native backend tests, and both manual-override regression tests passed. - Windows x64 GNU: workspace cross-target Clippy with all targets passed; neither new crate was compiled. title: fix(native): fall back to the release pages when the GitHub API fails
author: rishi29-cloud
body:
Fixes #875.

## The report

> Open the ArtCraft launcher on Windows 10. It tries to get available apps but marks every app as offline except the apps you already installed.

## Why that symptom means what it does

"Offline" is not a Windows check. `core::status::status` maps a lookup failure two different ways depending on whether the app is installed:

| | lookup failed |
|---|---|
| not installed | `AppStatus::Unavailable` → `tl!("Offline")` (`views.rs`, because `entry.failure().is_some()`) |
| installed | `AppStatus::Installed` → plain "Installed" |

So "every app offline except the ones I already have" is precisely "the release lookup returned `LatestRelease::Failed` for every app in the catalogue at once". There is no Windows-10-specific branch anywhere in the launcher; Windows 10 is simply where the reporter met it.

## Root cause

`GitHubSource::latest` gated the quota-free github.com release-pages route on `api_error.is_none()`:

```rust
if !prereleases && api_error.is_none() {
    match self.ask_pages(repo) { … }
}
```

That route was therefore taken **only** when GitHub explicitly answered "out of quota". Any real failure of the API request — no connection, a 403 or 407 carrying none of GitHub's rate-limit headers, a 5xx, an answer that couldn't be read — skipped it entirely and reported the app as failed.

`api.github.com` is a different host from `github.com`, and on a managed Windows machine it is usually the one that doesn't answer: a corporate firewall, a filtering DNS resolver or an HTTPS-inspecting proxy blocks the API while the release pages load perfectly well. The launcher had a working second route to the same information and declined to use it in exactly the situation it exists for.

## What changed

**`crates/native/src/source.rs`**

- The routing moved into a pure `resolve(repo, prereleases, limited, ask_api, ask_pages, cached)` that takes the three ways of asking as closures, in the same style as `backend::decide_fallback`, so the policy is …

title: native(install): probe /Applications with a randomly named file (#778)
author: ashokram-si
body:
Fixes #778

## What was wrong
On macOS, `applications_dir` decided between `/Applications` and `~/Applications` by writing an empty file named `.artcraft-launcher-write-test` into `/Applications` with `std::fs::write`. That opens with `O_CREAT | O_TRUNC`, so if the name is a symlink it follows it and truncates the target. `/Applications` is writable by every admin account, so another admin on the same Mac could plant that symlink and have the launcher empty a file the current user can write, the next time that user installs a Craft App for the first time (an update to an existing install, or an install to a chosen folder, doesn't reach this check).

## What changed
The check now calls `write_probe`, the helper that #925 added for the chosen-folder check in `crates/native/src/install.rs`: it creates a uniquely named file (`.artcraft-launcher-write-test-<pid>-<nanos>`) with `create_new` (`O_CREAT | O_EXCL`), which fails on any existing name, symlinks included, so nothing already in the folder is opened, followed or truncated, and removes it again. One helper for both probes, no new dependency and no `unsafe`.

I considered `access(W_OK)` instead, which writes nothing, but `std` has no safe wrapper and the workspace forbids `unsafe`, and creating a file checks exactly what the install does next.

## Tests
- `write_probe_leaves_a_planted_symlink_and_its_target_untouched`: plants a symlink at the old fixed name pointing to a file with content, runs the probe on a temp folder, and checks the file still has its content, the symlink is still there and nothing else is left. It fails with the old code (the file is emptied).
- `write_probe_reports_a_writable_folder_and_leaves_nothing_behind`: a writable folder gives `Ok` and stays empty; a missing folder gives `Err`.
- `write_probe_reports_a_read_only_folder_as_not_writable`: a `0555` folder gives `Err` (skipped when the tests run as root).

`write_probe` is not platform-gated, so these run on Linux CI too. They use temp folde…
