title: Accept exactly one download link per asset, and reject encoded traversal (#764)
author: smittie2000
body:
Closes #764.

## Summary

#764 reported that a download link could get past the "storytold only" check with `..` segments, written as `../` or percent-encoded as `%2e%2e/`. github.com resolves those segments before routing, so the link we checked isn't the one that gets served. Its suggested fix was to **accept exactly one link per asset**, built from the release's own tag and the asset's own name, and to check it again before downloading.

#747 already rejects literal `..`, extra path segments and `%2f`/`%5c`. This PR does the rest of what #764 asks:

| #764 asks for | Where it is now |
|---|---|
| Exactly one acceptable link per asset | `release::expected_download_url(repo, tag, name)` builds `https://github.com/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<name>`. The tag and name may only contain ASCII letters, digits and `._+-`. |
| Equality in `release_from_value` and `FeedRelease::to_release` | Both keep an asset only when its link equals that URL. This also ties the link to its release: an older release's file listed under a newer tag is dropped. |
| A check again just before fetching | `install::check_download_link`, called in `install_at` right before `download`. It catches a link into another app's releases with the right tag and name, which `bind_artifact_version` let through. |
| The mirror, since `%2e%2e` gets past `contains("..")` | `contains_encoded_separator` now rejects `%2e` as well as `%2f`/`%5c`. The loopback mirror check uses it. |

CodeRabbit found one more path in review. When the GitHub API is down, `release_from_sums` builds links from the names in `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and a name like `%2e%2e%2fother` passed `valid_file_name`. `valid_file_name` now rejects percent-encoded separators and dots, so every converter refuses such a name. `check_download_link` would catch the link too.

Every case needs control of a release or of the feed, so none of them is an open path traversal. They are the conditional supply-chain risk described in #764 and #90.

title: native(install): one prompt per run of system installs
author: nicholasgower
body:
Fixes #922.

On Linux, `pkexec` authenticates every call, so updating several apps at once asked for the password once per app. The Windows Craft-app MSIs are per-machine, so they asked for UAC once per app too. Both platforms now start one short-lived privileged helper and reuse it for the rest of the run.

## What changed

- **Linux:** the first system install or removal starts a helper through a single `pkexec`. Later package installs and removals go through it until it has been idle for fifteen minutes or the launcher exits. The helper runs only the fixed package-manager commands, requires install targets to be downloaded package files owned by the approving user, and accepts plain package names for removals.
- **Windows:** the first MSI install/removal starts the launcher again as an elevated helper through one `ShellExecuteEx` `runas` prompt. Later MSI installs and removals are sent over a loopback TCP connection. Packages are streamed to the helper and verified against their SHA-256, so the elevated account never reads the user's cache (including when UAC uses another administrator's credentials). The helper accepts only streamed MSIs and product-code removals.
- FreeBSD keeps its per-command `pkexec` prompt: its two root operations are not package-manager sessions.
- AppImage builds, the Flatpak sandbox, portable ZIPs, and the launcher's own per-user MSI self-update keep their existing paths.
- New Linux-only dependencies: `rustix` for SO_PEERCRED and `libc` for O_NOFOLLOW. Windows adds no crates; loopback TCP uses `std::net`, hashing uses the existing `sha2`, and `winsafe` gains its `shell` and `advapi` features.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native`: 187 passed
- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native -p artcraft-launcher --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo xtask wasm`
- The Windows code was type-checked and clippy-checked for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` against the real `winsafe` API. It has not been run…

title: Detection: a user Flatpak install is read before a system one (#881)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #881

## What was wrong
On a machine where an app is installed both system-wide and per-user, `flatpak list --app` lists both. `packages::find` takes the first match, which was the system copy. The launcher compared the latest release against that stale system version, so it kept offering an update it had already installed for the user. The comments on the issue confirm this: removing the system copy makes the update badge go away.

## What changed
`linux::packages()` in `crates/native/src/detect.rs` now runs `flatpak list --app --user` and then `--system`, so the user copy comes first and `find` picks it. The fallback `flatpak info` for bundles without a version uses the same scope, so it reads the copy that was listed. As the reporter suggested, a system-only install is still detected the same way.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native`: 169 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- Not tested on a machine with both a user and a system install. The change only reorders two `flatpak` calls whose output the existing parser already handles.

author: overprivileged

With **Check for updates: Only when I ask** (`check_every = Never`), the launcher still looked for updates once on every start: the first frame in `LauncherUi::logic()` always sent `CheckForUpdates { force: false }`. The timer below it already respects the setting; the startup check didn't.

title: fix(installer): Open fails with "X isn't where it was installed (X)" on MSI installs
author: Jeremy8776
body:
## Problem
After #925, an app installed by its MSI could not be opened: the toast said "DeckCraft isn't where it was installed (DeckCraft)".

Cause: the app's Windows Installer record was per-machine (HKLM) with no install folder recorded, but its files were in the user's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\<App>` folder. The scope-strict exe search only looks in the record's own scope, found nothing, and detection stored the bare app name as the location. Open then tried to run that name.

## Fix
- `detect.rs`: when the scoped search finds no exe, fall back to the suite folder under any install root. This only picks the exe that Open runs. The record's scope, which decides how updates run, is unchanged.
- `install.rs`: a bare-name location now gives a clear message instead of a fake path.
- Test: an exe in the suite folder of any root is found.

## Checked
`cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native --lib detect::` passes (13 of 13). Reproduced on a machine with a per-machine DeckCraft 0.12.0 record and files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\DeckCraft`. No full CI run locally.

---

title: Honor CARGO_BUILD_TARGET in FreeBSD packaging for aarch64 release builds
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Root cause
The shared release workflow (`craft-common-actions`) now builds FreeBSD aarch64 archives by default. title: feat(updater): update all-users Craft Apps without a permission prompt each time
author: Jeremy8776
body:
## What this does

Updating an app installed for all users (Program Files) asks Windows for permission every time. This adds an **optional** way around that: a small Windows service, installed once (one permission prompt), that does those updates for the launcher. Nobody is ever blocked. If the service is missing, stopped, or says no, the launcher does exactly what it does today.

Four commits, in order:

1. `crates/updater-service`: the service. The caller names only an app and a version. The service fetches the release from `storytold` itself, and refuses unless the app is in the catalog, installed for all users (read from Windows Installer's own machine record, not the uninstall entry, which exists for per-user installs too), older than the request, inside Program Files, named exactly, matching `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and validly Authenticode-signed by the publisher the certificate already carries (`Learning Machines Inc`, exact match). Anything it can't do safely (for example an install in `D:\Apps`) is a distinct "declined" reply, not an error.
2. `crates/updater-client` + `native::silent_update`: the launcher's side. The pipe code both sides share lives in the small client crate (the service depends on `native`, so `native` can't depend on the service). In `install_at`, before any download, and only for an MSI update with `MsiScope::PerMachine`, the launcher asks the service. Only "installed" ends the job. Everything else carries on with the existing download and `msiexec` route.
3. `packaging/windows/artcraft-updater.wxs`: a **separate** per-machine MSI that installs the service. The launcher's own MSI is not touched and stays per-user. No custom actions, the folder can't be redirected from the command line, and it is stopped and removed on uninstall. `check-updater-policy.ps1` reads the compiled tables; fixtures for x64, x86 and arm64 are built and checked in packaging lint.
4. Real-installer test scripts (elevated, undone afterwards).

Two Windows installer fixes on one slice: fresh app installs go machine-wide into `Program Files\ArtCraft\<App>`, and the UI now shows that real default folder instead of the words "System default".

## 1. Install new Windows apps for everyone (ace492b)

A fresh MSI install now asks Windows Installer for the machine-wide context (`ALLUSERS=1`) instead of taking the package's own default, which for a dual-scope package is per-user (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\<App>`). The install-folder fields (the per-app Install dialog and Settings' Default install folder) said "System default". They now show the folder a fresh install really uses:

- Windows portable ZIP: the launcher's own `apps` data folder

- Where no single default exists (web build, Linux system packages, FreeBSD): "System default" stays

The same value is the start folder of Browse, so it no longer opens at the literal string. Mechanism: `native::install::default_folder()` answers through a new `Host::default_install_folder()`, with no new translatable strings (no catalog churn).

title: feat(install): one permission prompt for an Update all of all-users apps on Windows
author: Jeremy8776
body:
## What this does

**Update all** on Windows now asks for permission once for every app installed for all users, instead of once per app.

Each all-users update downloads and checks its package against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` as before, then waits until the others of the same run are ready. One elevated PowerShell session (one permission prompt) then runs each package's fixed `msiexec` command line in turn. The session is given only those command lines, for packages the launcher has already checked, and it ends with the run. Nothing privileged stays installed or running, and the launcher itself is never started elevated.

- A batch of one keeps the existing route: `msiexec` asks for permission itself.
- If PowerShell cannot start, each package runs as before, with its own prompt.
- Per-user updates, fresh installs and removals are unchanged.

Relates to #922. Community PR #923 targets the same prompt with a long-lived elevated helper; this is a smaller alternative for Windows only.

## What was run for real

On a Windows 11 PC, with FilmCraft, GridCraft and WordCraft each set back one release and installed for all users, then **Update all** in a build of this change:

- One permission prompt. The launcher logged `updating 3 all-users apps under one permission prompt`.
- Each package's verbose MSI log shows it ran already elevated (no `consent provided` line) and ended with `MainEngineThread is returning 0`.
- All three ended on the new version with one machine-wide registration each. Settings under `%APPDATA%` were untouched.

Tests: `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native --lib` (including real PowerShell runs of the generated script with `cmd.exe` standing in for `msiexec`), `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. Linux-target clippy for `native` was not run locally (it needs a Linux C toolchain); CI covers it.

## Not covered

- The permission prompt names Windows PowerShell as the program, not ArtCraft…

title: fix(installer): Open fails with hive-mismatched MSI InstallDir (WordCraft/GridCraft)
author: endeprys
body:
## Problem

After installing Craft apps from ArtCraft Launcher on Windows (reproduced on **v0.9.0** with WordCraft and GridCraft), the hub shows the apps as installed and offers **Open**, but Open fails with:

> `WordCraft isn't where it was installed (WordCraft)`
> `GridCraft isn't where it was installed (GridCraft)`

The path in parentheses is the bare app name, not a filesystem path. **Show in folder** also fails (it isn't a file on this computer). The exes are present and launch fine from Explorer, e.g. under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\<App>\`.

Same class of reports: #970, #981, #985, #986 (and related). Primary Open fix landed in #954 but is **not in the v0.9.0 release** (merged after the tag).

### Root cause

Dual-scope Windows MSIs often split registry state across hives:

| Record | Typical location | Contents |
|--------|------------------|----------|
| Uninstall product | `HKLM\...\Uninstall\{GUID}` | `DisplayName` / version; **empty `InstallLocation`** |
| Install folder | `HKCU\SOFTWARE\<App>\InstallDir` | Real folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\<App>\` |
| App Paths | `HKCU\...\App Paths\<app>.exe` | Full path to the exe |

Launcher 0.9.0 resolves the exe **only in the uninstall record's hive**. For an HKLM uninstall row it looks for `InstallDir` / App Paths / Program Files under HKLM, finds nothing, and stores the bare name (`WordCraft`). Open then tries to run that name and errors.

A machine-side workaround that confirms this: writing `HKLM\SOFTWARE\<App>\InstallDir` to the real folder (as in a local `.reg` for FigCraft) makes Open succeed without moving files.

## Solution (this PR)

Builds on #954's launch fallback (`exe_in_any_scope`) so Open keeps working when the scoped lookup fails, and tightens the install/detect path so new hub installs are less likely to stay broken:

1. **`detect.rs` — App Paths in the cross-hive launch fallback**
   After trying `InstallDir` from every hive, also read `App Paths` from every hive/view b…

title: native, core: take desktop entries, package listings, the install queue and asset architectures from craft-update
author: smittie2000
body:
**Stacked on #930. Draft until #930 and storytold/craft-libs#424 merge.** #930's branch is on a fork, so GitHub's diff here includes #930's commits. This PR's own change is one commit: [compare `refactor/use-craft-update...refactor/drop-launcher-copies`](https://github.com/smittie2000/craft-launcher/compare/refactor/use-craft-update...refactor/drop-launcher-copies).

## Why

title: feat(versions): choose an app's or the launcher's version, with a one-prompt Windows downgrade
author: Jeremy8776
body:
## What this does

People can choose which version of an app, or of the launcher, they run: the latest release, the newest nightly build, or an exact older release. Going back is a deliberate choice, so the launcher then stops offering updates for that app.

**Choosing**
- Each app's **⋯** menu has **Choose version**. The launcher's own choice is a **Launcher version** dropdown in **Settings → Updates**.
- The list is the app's published releases (newest 100, from GitHub, cached 15 minutes). The newest stable one reads `v0.17.0 (latest release)`; choosing it follows new releases, as before.
- **Nightly** is offered only for a release with an explicit `-nightly` tag and a published checksum, never for any beta. It shows as `Nightly (none published yet)`, disabled, when there is none.
- A choice made in the dialog is a draft. The dialog's own **Install version {tag}** button keeps it; Close, Escape or a click outside puts the previous choice back.

**Kept versions don't nag**
- For an app kept on an exact version, the update check reports that release, so a newer one never shows as an update: no badge, no **Update all** entry, no notification, no automatic install.
- Its card and table row note the newer release quietly, in grey: `v0.16.0 · latest 0.17.0`.
- `ReleaseSource::chosen`'s default now answers pins and nightly from `versions()`; before, only the GitHub source did, and any other source silently dropped a pin.

**Going back on Windows**
- `install_at` refused every downgrade, and the app MSIs refuse to install over a newer copy. A version chosen by name below the installed one now:
  1. finds the installed version's own published release, and downloads and checks both packages before anything changes (without them, nothing is removed);
  2. removes the installed copy;
  3. installs the chosen version in the same folder and context, and reinstalls the previous one if that fails.

title: Fix RISC-V glibc requirements in Linux packages
author: skylartaylor
body:
The RISC-V release is built on Ubuntu 24.04 and needs glibc 2.39, but the Linux package template still declares `libc6 >= 2.35`. The shared release workflow already supplies `GLIBC_FLOOR=2.39`; this makes the packager use it for both deb and RPM dependencies, retaining 2.35 when the variable is unset or empty.

The mismatch is reproducible in the published 0.9.0 RISC-V deb: its checksum matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`, its control metadata declares 2.35, and the binary's ELF version requirements include `GLIBC_2.39`.

Adds a no-app-build CI regression check that runs the real Linux packager on fixture binaries and inspects the resulting deb/RPM dependencies for x64 and ARM64 defaults, the RISC-V override, an empty variable, and a custom override.

Validation:
- Real nFPM 2.47.0 fixture packages: deb/RPM requirements verified for x64 and ARM64 at 2.35, RISC-V at 2.39, and an explicit 2.40 override (8 packages).
- Baseline control reproduces the old deb 2.35 declaration and missing RPM glibc floor with `GLIBC_FLOOR=2.39`.
- Shellcheck, actionlint, Bash syntax and `git diff --check` pass.
- [Packaging CI](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/actions/runs/40930586243) passed: all 5 end-to-end deb/RPM cases, shared packaging lint, and Windows installer-policy fixtures.
- No Rust source, dependencies, version bump, or release trigger changes.

title: fix(install): reinstall a Flatpak bundle by hand on Flatpak before 1.16.2 (#909)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #909.

## Problem

On Flatpak older than 1.16.2, `flatpak install --reinstall --bundle` doesn't reinstall. There, `flatpak_dir_install_bundle` takes no reinstall flag and fails with `FLATPAK_ERROR_ALREADY_INSTALLED` when the bundle's commit is already deployed; `--noninteractive` prints that as `Failed to install bundle X: X already installed`, the error in the report. Flatpak added bundle reinstall in 919d2922 (1.17.0) and backported it to 1.16.2 as 4c5693b8. Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22 package 1.14.6; Mint 21 has 1.12.7, Debian 12 has 1.14.10.

The launcher installs the same commit again in two cases:

- **Reinstall** on an up-to-date Flatpak app. On those versions it fails every time.
- **Update** when the app also has an older system-wide copy. `flatpak list` puts the system copy first, so after an update into `--user` the launcher still offers one (#881), and the next click installs the same commit. The reporter says updating from the terminal asks for a password, which points to a system copy.

Both log `starting update to X`, so the log alone can't tell them apart.

## Fix

When the bundle install fails with Flatpak's `<id> already installed` and the host Flatpak is older than 1.16.2, the launcher uninstalls the user's copy and installs the bundle again. The install runs Flatpak in the C locale so that error reads the same on every system; on 1.14.6 it means the user's installation already has the bundle's commit (`flatpak_dir_install_bundle`). Any other failure, such as a bundle Flatpak can't load, leaves the installed copy alone. `--delete-data` isn't passed, so `~/.var/app/<id>` stays. Newer Flatpak does the same thing for `--reinstall`. Both steps run inside the installer queue, because an uninstall racing another bundle install can drop that bundle's `-origin` remote (#326).

Nothing changes on Flatpak 1.16.2 or later, or when the first install succeeds, except that Flatpak's own error text in the launcher's message is now English (the launcher'…

Follows #1007. Going back to an older version now works for a macOS app the launcher installed from its DMG, not only for Windows Installer copies.

title: fix(ui): keep the custom title bar's buttons above dialogs (#853)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #853.

## Problem

With the custom title bar (Windows and Linux), the first click on the header's Close does nothing while a dialog is open; the second click closes the window. Minimize and Maximize behave the same way.

A dialog is an egui `Modal`, whose backdrop fills `ctx.content_rect()`, header included. egui gives input only to layers at or above the top modal (`Memory::allows_interaction`), so the first click lands on the backdrop and dismisses the dialog. Only the second one reaches the button.

The likeliest way to meet this is the launcher-update prompt. While a newer launcher is out and automatic updates are off, it opens at every start (`on_launcher_update` keeps `fresh` only in memory), so closing an outdated launcher takes two clicks. Whether the reporter had it open is a guess; the report doesn't say.

## Fix

While a modal blocks the header (`Memory::is_above_modal_layer`), `window_buttons` draws its row in a tooltip-order layer through `UiBuilder::layer_id`, above the backdrop, as a system title bar would be. One click on Close then closes the window, and the dialog is still there when the window comes back. The rest of the time the buttons stay in the header exactly as on main.

The app details drawer and the screenshot lightbox also cover the header, but they keep main's behaviour on purpose: their own controls can sit under the caption buttons. The lightbox's Close is at x 1070-1104, y 16-50 in a 1120-wide window, right under the window's Close, and an app's menu can open up into that corner too. A first version of this PR lifted the buttons over everything, and CodeRabbit caught that it made the lightbox's Close close the window.

The row uses `UiBuilder::layer_id` rather than an `Area`: a new area spends its first frame on an invisible sizing pass, which would hide the buttons for a frame the first time a dialog opens.

- New `close_button_closes_with_a_dialog_open` opens Settings with the header's own button, then one click on C…

title: fix(core): tighten tag, file name and notice link checks (#776, #782)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Refs #776, #782.

## What changes

Only `crates/core`: `release.rs` and `feed.rs`.

1. **Tags** (#776, item 4). The new `release::valid_tag` is the rule `tag_from_redirect` already used (up to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._+-]`, not starting with a dot), now applied to GitHub's `tag_name`, the download link check and the feed's tag as well. This matters for the feed. On main, the feed tag `v0.6.0~beta-` followed by U+202E (right-to-left override) comes through as release 0.6.0-beta, because `version::parse` drops everything after the first `-` once it sees a `~`. With this change, that release gets `AskGitHub`, like any other feed release that doesn't hold up.
2. **File names** (#782, Validation). `valid_file_name` uses the same allowlist, and it also refuses a trailing dot and Windows device names (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.msi`). Before, it let through `%`, `#`, spaces and bidi overrides.
3. **Notice links** (#776, item 1). Feed notice links now go through `safe_web_link`. Release-note links already do. That drops plain `http://` and links with user-info, such as `https://getartcraft.com@evil.example/`.
4. **Notice cap** (#782, Input sizes). The 20-notice cap (`MAX_NOTICES`) is now applied after the rename notices are added, not before.

Items 2 and 3 of #776 are already fixed on main: release-page links refuse `.` and `..` (`safe_release_html_url`), and so do repo renames.

## Checked against real releases

I read the tags and asset names of the last 30 releases of all 14 catalog repos from the GitHub API on 2026-10-29, 4,832 names in all. Every one fits. None starts with a dot, and the live feed's 13 apps (365 asset names) pass too.

title: fix(native): no second self-update while the launcher restarts (#935, #782)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #935. Also covers one item of #782.

## A second self-update during the restart (#935)

`update_launcher` refused a second launcher update only while the first one was still in `jobs`, but the first one drops its job guard before it emits `LauncherRestarting`, and nothing checked `restarting`. So an `UpdateLauncher` that arrived after that point downloaded and staged the update again while the helper waited to swap in the first. If that second run failed, it also reset `restarting` (`backend.rs:440` on main), which let app installs start again before the restart.

`update_launcher` now also returns while `restarting` is set, as `start_job` already did.

Nothing sends that second command today. The egui front end keeps `launcher_job` set after a successful update until it quits, so neither the Update button nor `trigger_auto_updates` (`app.rs:736`) fires again, and no other front end sends backend commands. With this check the backend stops relying on that.

## `Instant::now() - 1 s` (#782, never-crash rule)

Both progress throttles, for the launcher's own update and for app jobs, started from `Instant::now() - Duration::from_secs(1)`. That subtraction panics if the monotonic clock reads under one second, and AGENTS.md rules out panics in non-test code. They now start from `None` (`Option<Instant>`), so there is no subtraction left and the first event always goes out. The rest of the `Instant` arithmetic in `native` is safe: it adds small constants, or the back-off in `http.rs`, which never exceeds 30 s.

## Tests

- New `no_second_launcher_update_starts_while_the_first_restarts`: with `restarting` set, `update_launcher` starts nothing and the flag stays set. On main it fails, because the second update runs and reports `JobFinished`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test (504 passed) and wasm all pass.

## Checked in the running app

title: fix(packaging): declare the launcher's real window class in its .desktop file (#1026)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #1026.

The launcher's window sets its Wayland app id and its X11 `WM_CLASS` to `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher` (`with_app_id(APP_ID)`, `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs:169`). The packaged entry has said `StartupWMClass=artcraft-launcher` since the first commit (ec69f0b), so the two never matched.

That only shows up when the entry has some other file name. GNOME Shell first looks for an entry whose `StartupWMClass` equals the window's class, and only then for `<class>.desktop`. The entry that AppRun and the .deb install is `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher.desktop`, so it is found by name. Entries written by AppImageLauncher or Gear Lever, or by hand, have another name, so nothing matched them: the dock showed a generic icon and the launcher couldn't be pinned.

The one-line change makes the declared class the real one, as `desktop_entry.rs` already does for the Craft apps (`StartupWMClass` = bundle id).

## Checked in GNOME Shell 50.1

I ran a headless `gnome-shell --headless` on a private D-Bus (scratch `HOME`, started as a `systemd-run --user` unit so no snap confinement leaks in), started the launcher on it, and read each window's matched app from `org.gnome.Shell.Introspect.GetWindows`:

| Entry in `~/.local/share/applications` | `StartupWMClass` | App GNOME matched |
|---|---|---|

title: AGENTS.md: CI workflows only call craft-common-actions at @main
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Adds a **CI workflows** section to the agent instructions (`AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` where it exists), so agents stop adding app-only CI:

- `.github/workflows/` only holds jobs that `uses:` a shared workflow from [storytold/craft-common-actions](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions), with its inputs and secrets. No inline `runs-on`/`steps` jobs, no app-only workflows.
- Always `@main`, never a SHA or tag.
- CI changes go into craft-common-actions; an app difference becomes an input to the shared workflow.
- Existing workflow files that predate the rule aren't extended, and their extra jobs move to craft-common-actions when touched.

Documentation only; no workflow is changed here. Several current workflows don't follow the rule yet (inline jobs beside the shared one in `packaging-lint.yml`, a SHA-pinned `windows-arm64.yml`), which is follow-up cleanup.

title: fix(packaging): no second menu entry when an AppImage manager already lists the launcher (#474, #394)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #474, fixes #394.

Builds on #1029: its commit is the first one here, and this one needs it (see below). Once #1029 is merged, only the second commit remains.

AppImage managers add their own menu entry for the AppImage under another file name: appimaged and AppImageLauncher write `appimagekit_<md5>.desktop`, and Gear Lever writes `artcraft_launcher.desktop`. AppRun then added `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher.desktop` beside it on every start, so the launcher was listed twice. Deleting the extra entry lasted until the next launch. #355 stopped this for Gear Lever when the launcher is started from Gear Lever's own entry (`DESKTOPINTEGRATION=1`). appimaged never sets that variable, and any other way of starting the file (a double click in the file manager, a terminal) still added the second entry.

## Change (`packaging/linux/AppRun`)

- `other_entry_runs` looks for an entry other than ours whose `[Desktop Entry]` group runs this exact AppImage and sets `StartupWMClass=ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher`. The path in `Exec=` has to be followed by a quote, a space or the end of the line, so an entry for `<path>.old` doesn't count. An `Exec=` in a `[Desktop Action]` group doesn't count either. One `grep -lF` over the user's entries narrows it down, so a normal start costs one extra process.
- When such an entry exists, AppRun installs nothing (no entry, no icons) and removes the entry it wrote on an earlier start, but only when `own_entry` says it is ours and unchanged. A renamed or otherwise edited entry stays.
- `own_entry` also accepts an entry whose only difference is the old `StartupWMClass=artcraft-launcher`. Every release since 0.6.0 wrote that body (the packaged entry hasn't changed since ec69f0b), so without this, everyone upgrading from those releases would keep their duplicate. It also means the normal refresh now updates the class line in existing entries, which #1029 had left as it was.

title: fix(ui): find the host's CJK fonts inside the Flatpak sandbox (#620)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #620.

The launcher looks for its Chinese and Japanese font at fixed host paths such as `/usr/share/fonts/noto-cjk/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc` (`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_font.rs`), but inside the Flatpak sandbox `/usr/share/fonts` is the runtime's own folder and the host's system fonts are mounted elsewhere (`add_font_path_args` in `common/flatpak-run.c`, read at tag 1.16.6):

| Host folder | In the sandbox |
|---|---|
| `/usr/share/fonts` | `/run/host/fonts` |
| `/usr/local/share/fonts` | `/run/host/local-fonts` |

Every lookup missed. The Flatpak build logged `no Chinese font found on this system` and showed English.

## Change

`candidates()` now follows each path under one of those two folders with its `/run/host` twin, for the same family, so the preference order doesn't change. That's how storytold/photocraft#1204 fixed PhotoCraft. It mapped only `/usr/share/fonts`; the launcher's list also has `/usr/local/share/fonts` paths, so this maps that mount too.

User fonts (the MiSans folders from #378) get no twin. Both manifests grant `--filesystem=home`, so `~/.local/share/fonts` is already readable at its usual path. Outside a sandbox the extra paths don't exist, and each one costs a failed `stat` until a font is found.

## Checked

- New test `flatpak_host_fonts_follow_the_paths_they_mirror`, plus `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui --lib` (72 passed), clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`.
- The real Flatpak, using Ubuntu's Flatpak 1.16.6, the `org.freedesktop.Platform//26.08` runtime from Flathub and the v0.10.0 `artcraft-launcher-0.10.0-linux-x86_64.flatpak` bundle. The host has `/usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc`, and the launcher ran on X11 with a scratch `HOME`.

| v0.10.0 bundle | `zh-CN` | `no Chinese font found on this system` | English |

title: fix(launch): say so when an app quits right after it starts
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #753.

Clicking Open on an app that can't start did nothing visible. `spawn_detached` (`crates/native/src/process.rs:111` on main) sends the app's output to /dev/null, and its reaper thread drops the exit status, so the only error the launcher could show was a failure to spawn. In #753 (PDFCraft's AppImage in a Docker container without FUSE), the spawn succeeds. The AppImage runtime then prints "Cannot mount AppImage, please check your FUSE setup." and exits with status 127.

## Change

- `process::spawn_watched` starts a command like `spawn_detached` and calls back with the exit status when it exits in error within a given window. `spawn_detached` is now that with a zero window, so `open` and `reveal` behave as before (Explorer's error status after a successful open stays ignored).
- `install::launch` builds the command for each kind of install and starts it with a 10 s window. For that, `launch_binary` became `binary_command` and `opener` is public, so the macOS `open` path is watched too. Ten seconds leaves room for an app that fails during its own setup on a slow machine; few people close an app that quickly.
- The backend shows the message as the error toast a failed spawn already got (`Event::JobFinished` with `Err`). It stays quiet when a job for that app has started in the meantime, because `on_job_finished` would otherwise clear that job's progress in the UI.
- For an AppImage, when `/dev/fuse` is missing or neither `fusermount3` nor `fusermount` is on `PATH`, the message adds that FUSE isn't set up. Inside the Flatpak sandbox the host's devices aren't visible, so it doesn't guess there.

The toast then reads: "SoundCraft quit right after starting (exit status: 127). AppImages need FUSE to run, and it isn't set up on this system."

## Checked

- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, wasm).
- New tests: `process::run_tests::only_a_failure_within_the_window_is_reported` (exit 3 inside the window is reported; exit 0, and an exit after the window, …
